Chinese-American Daily News of June 5, 1940 :-

CHINESE RESISTANCE BECOMING INCREASINGLY STRONG : HATRED BY
JAPANESE PEOPLE TOWARDS THEIR GOVERNMENT IS INCREASING DAILY:
FEET DEEP IN THE MIRE AND UNABLE TO RETREAT : SERIOUS
REPERCUSSIONS LIKELY

The following are the points of the statement
made by the Japanese Premier Yonai on June 3 that are likely
to arouse the attention of Chinese circles :-
(1) Japanese foreign policy should be centred
on the disposal of the China Incident.
(2) The China policy originally decided upon
is to be adhered to and new instructions are to be issued to
General Abe on the basis of the result of the meeting held on
May 31 by the Board of Asia Development, ordering him to start
negotiations with the puppet regime for "fundamental terms"
with a view to realizing the object of Japan's invasion of
China.
(3) No recognition of the puppet regime by
Japan before Wang Ching-wei signs and concludes the "fundamental
terms."
Developments of this new stage will be decided
by future changes. With a view to ascertaining the recent
conditions, a reporter of the Dah Chung News Agency called on
a certain diplomat yesterday and secured the following
information from him :-
In the European war Japan's position is more
important than that of Italy. However, due to the fact that
her feet have gone so deep in the mire in China that she is not
in a position to retreat, she has completely lost her freedom
to deal with the future events of the world. That she is sorry
in her heart can be verified by the Japanese Press.
(1) Of late the Japanese newspapers have all
hoped for an early conclusion of the China Incident so that
page_data.zh:
1940年6月5日《中美日报》：

中国抵抗力日益增强：日本民众对其政府的仇恨与日俱增：深陷泥潭无法抽身：恐引发严重后果

以下是日本首相米内于6月3日发表的声明中可能引起中国各界关注的要点：
(1) 日本外交政策应以处理“中国事变”为中心。
(2) 坚持原定的对华政策，并根据东亚振兴委员会5月31日会议的结果，向阿部将军发布新指令，命令他与傀儡政权就“基本条款”开始谈判，以实现日本侵华的目标。
(3) 在汪精卫签署并达成“基本条款”之前，日本不予承认傀儡政权。
这一新阶段的发展将由未来的变化决定。为了查明近期情况，《大中社》记者昨日拜访了一位外交官，并从他那里获得了以下信息：
在欧洲战争中，日本的地位比意大利更重要。然而，由于她在中国陷得太深，无法抽身，她已完全失去了应对未来世界事态的自由。从日本报刊的报道可以证实，她内心深感懊悔。
(1) 最近，日本报纸都希望早日结束“中国事变”，以便

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Japan can adopt a positive policy as regards the European war.
(2) The Asahi has frankly advised the Japanese
people to rid themselves of the yoke of the China Incident.
However, the Japanese militarists have failed
to come to their senses. Following defeats in military
operations, they have started political attacks; not only
are they desiring to beat China to her knees, but they are
also attempting to conquer the whole of China. They are
planning to make use of Wang Ching-wei, the puppet, to bring
about the annexation of Manchuria and Mongolia, the blockade
of Central China, the control of South China and the whole of
this country from Heilungkiang in the north to Hainan Island
in the south, from the coast to the creeks in the interior,
etc. They intend to convert the accomplished facts into terms
and law.
The Chinese Government, in its desire to secure
the integrity of its territory and the sovereignty of its
administrative rights, naturally is unable to allow herself
to be conquered or slaughtered by Japan. Consequently, it
is determined to carry on the war of resistance without entering
into peace with Japan until the Japanese forces have been driven
from Chinese soil. Finding it impossible to effect the
conquest of China, Prince Konoye, the ex-Premier of the Japanese
Government, advocated the continuation of war against China
until the collapse of the Chinese National Government. However,
as a result of resistance in the past three years, China has
become more united politically and stronger militarily. What
Prince Konoye said has still failed of materialisation up to
the present. On the contrary, Japan is facing a poorer
situation gradually, while her people have become gradually
more displeased with their government. It is for this reason
that the "Kokumin" recently expressed its hope for an early
solution of the China Incident and that the government would
not use superficial means to bring about an incomplete solution
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

日本能对欧洲战争采取积极政策。
(2) 《朝日新闻》坦率地建议日本人民摆脱“中国事变”的枷锁。
然而，日本军国主义者并未清醒过来。继军事行动失败后，他们开始了政治攻击；他们不仅希望迫使中国屈服，还试图征服整个中国。他们计划利用傀儡汪精卫来实现吞并满洲和蒙古、封锁华中、控制华南以及控制从北部的黑龙江到南部的海南岛、从沿海到内陆河流等整个国家的目的。他们打算将既成事实转化为条款和法律。
中国政府为了维护领土完整和行政主权，自然不能允许自己被日本征服或屠杀。因此，它决心进行抗战，直到日军被赶出中国国土之前，不与日本议和。鉴于无法实现征服中国的目的，日本政府前首相近卫文麿主张继续对华作战，直至中国国民政府崩溃。然而，经过过去三年的抵抗，中国在政治上更加团结，军事上更加强大。近卫所说的话至今仍未成为现实。相反，日本的处境逐渐恶化，而其民众对政府的不满也日益增加。正因如此，《国民新闻》最近表示希望早日解决“中国事变”，并且在中国国民政府进行抗战之际，政府不应使用表面手段促成不彻底的解决，

page_data.en:
- 3 -

at this time when the Chinese National Government is carrying
on its war of resistance, because what the people want is a
complete peace and not a partial one.
This is what the Japanese people hope for from
their government and yet the latter is working contrary to
their expectations. It can be very well expected that this
will give rise to serious repercussions.
Conflict between General Abe and Wang Ching-wei -
Negotiations break down
The most important mission of General Abe as
Envoy Extraordinary to Nanking is to carry into force the
statement of Prince Konoye and to draw up "fundamental terms"
with Wang Ching-wei. Following the arrival of General Abe,
Wang Ching-wei planned to commence the negotiations after the
presentation of credentials by General Abe. Prior to General
Abe's coming to China, Wang Ching-wei had various rites
rehearsed in order to be prepared for the receiving of General
Abe. However, General Abe paid a call on Wang Ching-wei at
the latter's residence and insisted that he would not present
his credentials until an agreement between the Japanese and the
puppets had been signed. The views of the two sides reached
an impasse and a serious split occurred. Recently, Admiral
Yonai declared that fresh instructions would be sent to General
Abe to resume the talks but the recognition of the puppet regime
would be given only after the amelioration of the "fundamental
terms." Wang Ching-wei is worrying as to whether Japan will
carry out this "superficial procedure."
Not one demand of Wang Ching-wei accepted
Recently Wang Ching-wei appointed Chen Kung-po,
Chu Min-yi and others to proceed to Japan ostensibly to return
his respects but in reality to ascertain the true intention of
the Japanese and to request the Japanese to give immediate
recognition. It is learned that Chen Kung-po has submitted
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

因为人民想要的是完全的和平，而不是部分的和平。
这是日本人民对政府的期望，但后者却违背了他们的期望。可以预见，这将引发严重的后果。
阿部将军与汪精卫之间的冲突——谈判破裂
阿部将军作为驻南京特命全权大使的最重要使命，是执行近卫公爵的声明，并与汪精卫起草“基本条款”。阿部将军抵达后，汪精卫计划在阿部将军递交国书后开始谈判。在阿部来华之前，汪精卫排练了各种仪式，以准备接待阿部将军。然而，阿部将军前往汪精卫寓所拜访，并坚持在日伪双方签署协议之前不递交国书。双方观点陷入僵局，发生了严重分裂。最近，米内海军上将宣布将向阿部将军发送新指令以恢复谈判，但只有在改善“基本条款”后才会给予傀儡政权承认。汪精卫正担心日本是否会履行这一“表面程序”。
汪精卫的要求无一被接受
最近，汪精卫任命陈公博、褚民谊等人前往日本，名义上是回访致意，实则是探明日本的真实意图，并要求日本立即予以承认。据悉，陈公博已向

page_data.en:
- 4 -

the following three demands to the Japanese :-
(1) Immediate recognition of the puppet regime.
(2) Permission to train its own army.
(3) Establishment of a "Central Bank."

It is said that Chen Kung-po's efforts have proved futile and that he will return in low spirits.

As regards the first request, the Japanese pretence is that she will give recognition when she has completed the necessary arrangements among the Powers.

The second request cannot be accepted because the greatest danger of the training of an army is that once this army turns coat, it is likely to bolster up the influence of the guerrillas.

In connection with the third request, the Japanese have suffered heavily following their establishment of the Federal Reserve Bank in North China and of the Hwa Shing Bank in Central China, resulting in the heavy drop in the value of the Japanese banknotes and affecting seriously Japan's trade abroad. For the present, the Japanese are unwilling to increase their burden any more and on this account they have turned down the request.

This shows that the only hope Japan holds of Wang Ching-wei is to conclude a treaty for the sale of China through the hands of Wang Ching-wei. One can imagine what the future holds for the puppet regime. --- Dah Chung News Agency.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

日本提出了以下三项要求：
(1) 立即承认傀儡政权。
(2) 允许训练自己的军队。
(3) 建立“中央银行”。

据说陈公博的努力证明是徒劳的，他将情绪低落地返回。

关于第一项要求，日本的借口是，当她在列强之间完成必要的安排后，将给予承认。

第二项要求不能被接受，因为训练军队的最大危险在于，一旦这支军队倒戈，可能会助长游击队的影响。

关于第三项要求，日本在华北设立联合准备银行和在华中设立华兴银行后遭受了重大损失，导致日本纸币价值大幅下跌，严重影响了日本的对外贸易。目前，日本不愿再增加负担，因此拒绝了这一要求。

这表明，日本对汪精卫唯一的希望是通过汪精卫之手签订出卖中国的条约。人们可以想象傀儡政权的未来。——大中社。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY

MAY 2, 1940

The Readers'
Forum

Jewish Refugees

To the Editor:
My attention has been directed
to a paragraph contained in your
journal, stating that probably 3,000
Central European refugees would
be landing in Shanghai in the
course of the current month. As
a member of the Refugee Com-
mittee, in charge of affairs per-
taining to immigration, I must
stigmatize this statement as a gross
exaggeration. To my estimation
the number of immigrants likely
to land here in May will be much
nearer to 30, than to 3,000. The
total of Central European immi-
grants at present residing here
also is being grossly exaggerated,
for it is nearer 19,000 (after 21
months of immigration) than 27,-
000 and more, as insinuated by a
portion of the local press.
Yours faithfully,
E. KANN
Shanghai, May 26, 1940.

With all due regard for Mr.
Kann's position and informa-
tion, we call attention to the
point made by municipal offi-
cials that only arrivals with
less than U.S.$400 are requir-
ed to have refugee permits.--
EDITOR.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》

1940年5月2日

读者
论坛

犹太难民

致编辑：
我注意到贵刊中的一段文字，称本月内可能有3,000名中欧难民抵达上海。作为负责移民事务的难民委员会成员，我必须指出这一说法是严重的夸大。据我估计，5月份可能抵达这里的移民人数更接近30人，而非3,000人。目前居住在这里的中欧移民总数也被严重夸大，实际数字更接近19,000人（经过21个月的移民），而非当地部分媒体暗示的27,000人以上。
此致
敬礼，
E. KANN
上海，1940年5月26日。

尽管我们充分尊重坎恩先生的地位和所提供的信息，但我们提请读者注意市政官员指出的这一点：只有携带少于400美元的人需要难民许可证。——编辑。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
MAY 26 1940

Number Nearer 30
CommitteeMan
Denies 3,000
Jews Due Here

The report that 3,000 Jewish refugees are expected to arrive here in the near future was stigmatized as a "gross exaggeration" yesterday by Mr. E. Kann, member of the Refugee Committee, who said that the number of the new arrivals is much nearer 30.

Mr. Kann estimated that there are at present about 19,000 emigres living in Shanghai.

The report of the large new influx of refugees from Nazidom was obviously denied by Mr. Ellis Hayim, chairman of the committee currently granting aid to new arrivals, and by Municipal Police officials dealing with the immigration of refugees here.

Since wholesale immigration of Jewish refugees into Shanghai was stopped about six months ago, the majority of fresh arrivals have permits for residence in the Settlement only. Few permits are being issued for residence in the Concession, and an insignificant number by Japanese authorities north of Soochow Creek.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。
1940年5月26日

人数接近30人
委员
否认3,000名
犹太人即将抵沪

难民委员会成员E. Kann先生昨日指责有关近期将有3,000名犹太难民抵达这里的报道是“严重夸大”，他说新抵达的人数更接近30人。

Kann先生估计，目前约有19,000名流亡者居住在上海。

来自纳粹统治区的大批新难民涌入的报道显然遭到了目前正在向新抵达者提供援助的委员会主席Ellis Hayim先生以及负责处理这里难民移民事务的警务处官员的否认。

自从大约六个月前停止犹太难民大规模移民上海以来，大多数新抵达者仅持有在租界居住的许可证。发放给在公共租界居住的许可证很少，而苏州河以北的日本当局发放的数量更是微不足道。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS
MAY 25 1940

Arrival Here
Of 3,000 Jews
Expected Soon

The local European Jewish
emigre colony, which numbers
a total of approximately 20,000,
is expected to swell considerably
with the arrival here early next
month of a new batch of re-
fugees numbering 3,000, it was
rumored yesterday.

A large number of the new
arrivals are expected on the Lloyd
Tristino liner, Conte Verde, which
is due in port on June 6.

Mr. Ellis Hayim, chairman of the
committee currently granting aid to
the emigres, yesterday denied all
knowledge of the arrival of a new
batch of refugees, however.

The Shanghai Municipal Council
and the police officials dealing with
refugee immigration here, also
stated that they knew nothing of
the new arrivals.

According to the restrictions
promulgated by the S.M.C. and the
Japanese authorities here, it is
possible for refugees to take up
residence in Shanghai if they
present a sum of US$400 at their
arrival. Entry into the city is also
allowed those with relatives here,
who are able to support them dur-
ing their stay.

There is a large number of
refugees who have already estab-
lished themselves here, in posses-
sion of businesses, boarding houses,
shops and restaurants, and those
who have found jobs, who would
consequently be able to support
relatives.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1940年5月25日

三千名犹太人
预计即将抵沪

据昨日传闻，目前本地欧洲犹太难民群体总数约为两万人，预计下月初将有一批新的难民抵达，人数达三千人，这将使该群体规模大幅膨胀。

预计大批新抵达者将乘坐劳埃德·特里斯蒂诺轮船公司（Lloyd Tristino）的“康特·维尔德”号（Conte Verde）轮，该轮定于6月6日抵港。

然而，目前负责向难民提供援助的委员会主席埃利斯·海姆（Ellis Hayim）先生昨日否认知晓新一批难民抵达之事。

上海公共租界工部局及负责此处难民移民事务的警务官员也表示，他们对新抵达者一事毫不知情。

根据上海公共租界工部局与驻沪日本当局颁布的限制规定，难民若在抵达时出示400美元，即可在上海居住。此外，若有在沪亲属并能由其资助在华期间的生活费用，亦获准入境。

已有大量难民在此立足，他们拥有企业、寄宿公寓、商店和餐馆，或已找到工作，因此有能力资助其亲属。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.

MAY 25 1940

REPORT OF REFUGEE
ARRIVALS DENIED

S.M.P. Say Permits Not
Issued To 3,000
More Emigres

The report that 3,000 Jewish re-
fugees are coming to Shanghai by
the end of this month and that
permits have been issued to all of
them by the Shanghai Municipal
Council, was denied by the S.M.P.
yesterday. They said that permits
had been issued to nothing like this
number of people and that it was
a physical impossibility that 3,000
refugees could arrive here during
the next week as there are no ships
coming.

However, the general impression
persists that a large number of
Jewish refugees from Europe are
coming to Shanghai soon, and these
possible new emigres include those
who have enough money not to need
S.M.C. permits. Restrictions, it
may be remembered, were placed
on further emigre arrivals here last
year. However, under these re-
strictions it is still possible for re-
fugees to land here without per-
mits if they possessed a sufficient
amount of money, the minimum
being U.S.$400.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》

1940年5月25日

否认难民抵达报告

工部局警务处称未向另外
三千名难民签发许可证

昨日，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）否认了有关三千名犹太难民将于本月底抵达上海，且上海公共租界工部局已向所有人签发许可证的报道。警方表示，签发的许可证数量远未达到此数，且由于近期无船只抵港，下周内不可能有三百名难民抵达，这在物理上是不可能的。

然而，普遍印象仍然是大量来自欧洲的犹太难民即将抵达上海，这些潜在的新移民中包括那些拥有足够资金、无需申请上海公共租界工部局许可证的人。需指出的是，去年已对进一步迁入此地的难民实施了限制。然而，在这些限制下，如果难民拥有足够资金（最低金额为400美元），仍可在无许可证的情况下在此登陆。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

1941

3,000 Refugees Due
Here Next Week

Increasing the existing number of Jewish refugees in Shanghai, at present estimated over 17,000, to a new total of over 20,000. 3,000 more Jewish refugees are expected to arrive in Shanghai from Europe towards the end of May, it was reported yesterday.
Permission is said to have been secured from the Shanghai Municipal Council for their arrival. It is estimated that of the huge number already in Shanghai, only 30 per cent. have secured employment.

将于下周抵沪

据报道，预计五月底将有另外三千名犹太难民从欧洲抵达上海，使目前估计超过一万七千人的在沪犹太难民总数增加至两万余人。

Shun Pao :-

3,000 JEWISH REFUGEES DUE IN SHANGHAI END OF MAY

The position of Jews has become more
difficult following the extension of the European war.
According to information secured from Jewish refugees,

May 23, 1940.

National Herald, Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao and
Min Van Pao :-

20 RICE DEALERS TO BE PROSECUTED

According to reliable information, the two
Municipal Councils will institute legal proceedings against
speculators next week. There are 20 rice merchants in the
International Settlement who are said to have failed to
mention the prices of their wares despite repeated warnings
by the S.M.C. Consequently, the S.M.C., as a deterrent to
others, has decided to institute a prosecution against these
20 rice merchants next week.
The Commodity Prices Control Committee of the
Council will detail officials to carry out an inspection of
shops in the district to ascertain whether the prices of
goods are being exhibited in accordance with the stipulations
of the Committee. The officials will also ascertain whether
these prices are proper or whether they have have raised.

It is said that in the past, shops in
close proximity to each other have frequently marked
different prices on similar articles, the difference in
prices being about $0.10. In connection with such cases,
the Council has decided to order those shops which are
charging a higher price to make adjustments voluntarily.
page_data.zh:
1940年5月23日。
下午译文。

《神州日报》、《中美日报》、《大美报》及
《民闻报》：-

二十名米商将被起诉

据可靠消息，两个市政委员会将于下周对投机商提起法律诉讼。据说国际租界内有20名米商尽管受到上海公共租界工部局的多次警告，仍未标明商品价格。因此，上海公共租界工部局为儆效尤，决定下周对这20名米商提起诉讼。
工部局物价管制委员会将派遣官员对该地区的商店进行检查，以确定商品标价是否符合委员会的规定。官员们还将核实这些价格是否合理，以及是否有涨价行为。

据说，过去彼此邻近的商店经常对类似商品标出不同的价格，价差约为0.10美元。针对此类情况，工部局决定命令那些收取较高价格的商店自愿进行调整。

MAY 23 1940

Twenty Profiteers Spotted
As Council Starts Purge

The Municipal Council yesterday brought its legal guns into action in its fight against profiteering in Shanghai. For the first time since the law came in force, 20 stall-holders will be prosecuted in court early next week for not exhibiting price-tags in front of their stalls, THE CHINA PRESS was informed.

This step was described by a member of the Price Control Committee as the "beginning of more energetic action" against profiteering in food and commodity prices here. In time, it was stated, similar action will be taken against store-owners refusing to exhibit price-tags, and, as additional evidence is received, merchants and dealers will be taken into court on the more serious charge of profiteering.

"Deeds, Not Words"

It was explained that legal action against the 20 stall-holders was taken after numerous warnings had been issued by the Council. This action was not taken before as sufficient time had to be allowed for all dealers to acquaint themselves with the procedure they were required to follow in selling their products.

Furthermore, it was stated, the dealers had to be given time to realize that the Council "meant what it said, and intended to follow up its words with deeds."

The French Municipal Council yesterday had not filed charges against any dealers. It was stressed, however, that the Settlement body's step was being carried out with the co-operation of the French Municipality, so that similar action in the Concession could be expected shortly.

Meanwhile, Council inspectors continued to visit markets and stores in the Settlement, and see that dealers followed the required regulations in selling their food.

False Scales Confiscated

THE CHINA PRESS was present on one of these inspection tours yesterday. The inspector made sure that every stall was exhibiting a price-tag in a prominent place, and confiscated a number of scales with incorrect measures.

Neighboring price-tags were often seen to bear different prices for the same product, the difference usually amounting to about 10 cents. Nothing was yet being done on the question of different price-scales, it was stated, as the Council had so far made no attempt to fix prices.

However, it was pointed out, a buyer seeing one price-tags bearing figures lower than another, would naturally make his purchases in the former stall, and this formed an incentive for dealers to lower their prices themselves.

Prices On Downtrend

Meanwhile, a downward trend in local food prices was experienced yesterday, explained by the recent improvement in the exchange value of the Chinese dollar.

Produce firms set the example in this trend, when both the Henning-sen Produce Company and the Geddes Trading and Dairy Farm Company announced a reduction of 1¢ per pound on their brands of butter. This brought the price of their butter down from $7.10 a pound to $6.10 a pound.

Several compradore stores cut their rates by amounts ranging from 10 per cent to 25 per cent. The Shanghai General Supply Company, 1041 Avenue Joffre, announced that, effective immediately, all their prices would be reduced by 15 per cent. A 10 per cent reduction was previously made on May 20, they pointed out.

Having already lowered their prices on May 19, the Van Shing grocery store, on Avenue Joffre, announced that further reduction came into effect yesterday.

The 50 per cent surcharge levied on all wines and spirits distributed by Goldstick, Macgregor and Company, was cancelled on Saturday. On the heels of this step, the Shanghai Municipal Council yesterday announced that all liquors made of alcohol had been reduced in price.

1940年5月23日

工部局开始整顿
查出二十名牟取暴利者

《字林西报》获悉，上海公共租界工部局昨日在其打击上海牟取暴利行为的斗争中动用了法律手段。自该法律生效以来，首次有20名摊主因未在摊位前展示价格标签，将于下周初被起诉出庭。

物价管制委员会的一名成员将此举措描述为对此地食品和商品价格牟取暴利行为采取“更有力行动”的“开端”。据悉，届时将对拒绝展示价格标签的店主采取类似行动，并且随着获得更多证据，商人及经销商将以更严重的牟取暴利罪名被带上法庭。

“重行动，轻言语”

据解释，在对这20名摊主采取法律行动之前，工部局已发出多次警告。此前未采取行动是因为必须给予所有经销商足够的时间，让他们熟悉销售产品所需遵循的程序。

此外，据悉，必须给予经销商时间，让他们意识到工部局“言出必行，并打算以行动兑现承诺。”

昨日，法公董局尚未对任何经销商提出指控。但强调指出，租界当局的这一行动是在法公董局的配合下进行的，因此预计法租界内不久也将采取类似行动。

与此同时，工部局视察员继续巡视租界内的市场和商店，确保经销商在销售食品时遵守相关规定。

没收不准秤具

《字林西报》记者昨日参加了其中一次视察。视察员确保每个摊位都在显眼位置展示了价格标签，并没收了一些计量不准的秤具。

经常可以看到相邻的价格标签对同一产品标出不同的价格，差额通常约为10美分。据悉，目前尚未对不同价格体系的问题采取行动，因为工部局迄今未试图固定价格。

然而，有人指出，买家看到一张价格标签上的数字低于另一张时，自然会在前者处购买，这形成了促使经销商自行降低价格的激励。

价格呈下降趋势

与此同时，昨日本地食品价格出现下降趋势，这被归因于近期中国货币汇率价值的改善。

农产品公司在此趋势中树立了榜样，亨宁森农产品公司（Henning-sen Produce Company）和盖迪斯贸易乳品农场公司（Geddes Trading and Dairy Farm Company）均宣布将其品牌黄油每磅降价1美分。这使其黄油价格从每磅7.10美元降至6.10美元。

几家买办商店将价格降低了10%至25%不等。位于霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）1041号的上海通用供应公司（Shanghai General Supply Company）宣布，即日起所有价格降低15%。他们指出，此前已于5月20日降价10%。

霞飞路的万兴杂货店（Van Shing grocery store）已于5月19日降价，昨日宣布进一步降价生效。

周六取消了对 Goldstick, Macgregor and Company 分销的所有葡萄酒和烈酒征收的50%附加费。紧随此举，上海公共租界工部局昨日宣布所有酒精饮料均已降价。

May 11, 1940.

Deputy Commissioner,
Special Branch,
S. M. P.

I beg to inform you that I have taken over the
Dah Chung News Agency since March 8, 1940. I failed
to apply for re-registration of my news agency at an
earlier date as I thought that such was not necessary
on the grounds that there was no indication on the
certificate issued to the former holder in respect
of the firm that the licence was issued to certain
designated persons nor was there any mention made on
its reverse side that the licence was not transferable.
I shall be much obliged if you will grant
re-registration of my news agency.

Chen Ting-huei.

1940年5月11日。

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

谨告知阁下，我自1940年3月8日起已接管大中通讯社。我未能更早申请通讯社的重新注册，是因为我认为此举并无必要，理由是发给前持有人的证书上并未指明执照是颁发给特定指定人员的，其背面也未提及执照不可转让。
如蒙批准我的通讯社重新注册，不胜感激。

陈廷辉。

S. P. REGISTER
Date Dec. 27, 1939
Subject. Dah Chung News Agency Temporarily Suspends Its Operations
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Golder.

The Dah Chung News Agency (大中通訊社, whose office is in Room 504 of the Chung Wei Banking Building, No.143 Avenue Edward VII, French Concession, has announced its temporary suspension as from December 25.

This news agency was formed in July last by Wu Chung-yih (吳中一), Chinese editor of the Ta Mei Pao (大美報), Chinese morning edition of the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury.

On December 16 a reporter of the agency named Chen Hsi-chang (or Zung Shien-tsang 陳憲章) was kidnapped on Nanking Road by the Wang Ching-wei clique but as he agreed to join the clique, he telephoned on the following day to the Sin Wan Pao (新聞報), the Chinese-American Daily News (中美日報), etc., denying any report published by local Chinese newspapers relating to his abduction. As a result of his joining Wang's clique, a threatening letter, enclosing with a bullet was sent to the residence of Wu Chung-yih, No.107 Hsin Ling Tsung (信陵邨), Rue du Marche, on December 23, while a telephone message was sent to Wu Chung-yih in the office of the Ta Mei Pao, demanding that he leave Shanghai within ten days. A report to this effect has been made to the French Police. Apart from temporarily suspending the operations of the Dah Chung News Agency, Wu Chung-yih is now nightly sleeping in the office of the Ta Mei Pao.

D. C. (Special Branch).

大中通讯社 (大中通訊社)，其办公室位于法租界爱多亚路143号中汇银行大楼504室，已宣布自12月25日起暂时停业。

该通讯社由去年七月成立，创办人为《大美报》(Ta Mei Pao) 的中文编辑吴中一 (吳中一)，《大美报》系《上海晚邮报与水星报》(Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury) 的中文版晨报。

12月16日，该社一名名为陈宪章 (Chen Hsi-chang 或 Zung Shien-tsang 陳憲章) 的记者在南京路被汪精卫派系绑架，但由于他同意加入该派系，次日便致电《新闻报》(Sin Wan Pao)、《中美日报》(Chinese-American Daily News) 等报社，否认本地中文报纸刊登的关于其被绑架的任何报道。由于其加入汪派，12月23日，一封夹带子弹的恐吓信被寄至吴中一位于市场路 (Rue du Marche) 信陵邨107号的住所，同时吴中一在《大美报》办公室接到电话留言，要求他在十天内离开上海。此事已向法国警察报案。除了暂时停止大中通讯社的运作外，吴中一现在每晚都睡在《大美报》的办公室里。

Ta Ying Yeh Pao dated December 26 :- 27.12.39(AM)
DAH CHUNG NEWS AGENCY SUSPENDS OPERATIONS
The Dah Chung News agency (大中社 ) was
established several months ago. It has been experiencing
much difficulty in handling its affairs since the
abduction of its reporter named Chen Hsi-ching (陳憲章)
which occurred recently in front of the Chocolate Shop
on Nanking Road. Consequently, the agency ceased
operations on the night of December 25.
Yours

《大英夜报》(Ta Ying Yeh Pao) 12月26日刊 :- 1939年12月27日(上午)
大中通讯社停止运作
大中通讯社 (大中社 ) 成立于数月前。自其记者陈宪章 (陳憲章) 近期在南京路巧克力店门前被绑架以来，该社在处理事务方面一直面临诸多困难。因此，该社于12月25日晚停止运作。

page_data.en:
December 22, 1939.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

ANTI-JAPANESE CHINESE NEWSPAPER REPORTER
JOINS PEACE MOVEMENT

Anti-Japanese journalists on
the south side of the creek whose conditions are
worsening are beginning to join Wang Ching Wei's
peace movement.
On December 16 a Chinese
journalist named Zung Shien Tsang, a correspondent
of the Dah Chung News Agency and concurrently a
clerk of the Chinese Newspaper Reporters' Lien Nyi
Association, joined the peace movement. This has
given rise to great unrest among the anti-Japanese
journalists.
The Dah Chung News Agency is
notoriously anti-Japanese, distributing anti-Japanese
propaganda with financial support from the Chung-
king Government.
Sung Shien Tsang is reported
to have left the News Agency because Lu Chung Ih,
manager of the concern was deliberately fabricating
anti-Japanese news when he knew that the war of
resistence cannot help China. Zung Shien Tsang's
joining with the peace movement has caused great
panic among the anti-Japanese journalists because
he knows Chungking's propaganda secrets. As a
result of Zung's disaffection Ching Hwa Ding of the
"Sun Pao", Chang Sz Hsueh, Chao Chuin Hao and Chui
Chao Ye of the "Dah Mei Wan Pao" and Lu Chung Ih,
manager of the Dah Chung News Agency, have held secret
meetings during the past few days to consider the
matter. It is further reported that Lu Kai Sien
is working behind them.
Lu Chung Ih is said to have
appealed to the French authorities for protection.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月22日。

《大陆新报》(TAIRIKU SHIMPO)

反日华报记者
加入和平运动

苏州河以南地区处境日益恶化的反日记者开始加入汪精卫的和平运动。
12月16日，一名名为宗先藏 (Zung Shien Tsang) 的中国记者，系大中通讯社通讯员，兼任中国新闻记者联谊会职员，加入了和平运动。这在反日记者中引起了极大的不安。
大中通讯社以反日著称，在重庆政府的财政支持下散布反日宣传。
据报道，宋先藏 (Sung Shien Tsang) 离开该通讯社是因为该社经理陆仲义 (Lu Chung Ih) 在明知抗战无助于中国的情况下，故意捏造反日新闻。宗先藏 (Zung Shien Tsang) 加入和平运动在反日记者中引起了极大恐慌，因为他知晓重庆的宣传机密。由于宗的背离，《申报》(Sun Pao) 的丁景华 (Ching Hwa Ding)、《大美晚报》(Dah Mei Wan Pao) 的张思学 (Chang Sz Hsueh)、赵俊豪 (Chao Chuin Hao) 和崔朝业 (Chui Chao Ye) 以及大中通讯社经理陆仲义 (Lu Chung Ih) 在过去几天举行了秘密会议商讨此事。另有报道称，卢凯仙 (Lu Kai Sien) 在幕后操纵。
据说陆仲义已向法国当局寻求保护。

page_data.en:
December 17, 1939. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao and
National Herald :-

POLITICAL ABDUCTION ON NANKING ROAD

At 9.05 p.m. yesterday an abduction of a
political nature occurred in front of the Chocolate Shop
on Nanking Road, in which one named Chen Hsi-chang (陳憲章 )
who was one time a clerk in the local Newspaper Reporters
Association, was forcibly carried off.
It appears that a person named Yuan Siao-yih
(袁肖逸 ) alias Yuan Hsueh-yen (袁學易 ), editor of the
former Wei Lung News Agency (魏龍社 ), has been attempting
to work harm in newspaper circles ever since his surrender
to the Wang Ching-wei clique. However, being not very well
acquainted with the members of the newspaper fraternity,
he has on several occasions invited Chen Hsi-chang for
consultations, hoping to induce the latter to act as his
informer, but each time he proved unsuccessful. Being hard
pressed by Yuan recently, Chen went to the Chocolate Shop
last night, intending to enlighten Yuan on the principles
of loyalty and righteousness. Fearing unexpected trouble,
Chen went to the place in company with several friends. On
arriving at the place, Chen noticed three private cars, the
licence numbers of two of which were 8021 and 4693, standing
in the front of the shop. Yuan at that time was standing
by the side of one of the cars. On seeing the approach of
Chen, he forced him into one of the vehicles which then left
at a high speed in a westerly direction followed by the
other two cars. It is believed that they were driven out
towards the Western District.

Chinese-American Daily News and Sin Wan Pao :-

REPORT OF ABDUCTION ON NANKING ROAD SAID UNTRUE

A person who claimed to be named Chen Hsi-chang
(陈锡章 ) has informed this paper by telephone that the
report published in newspapers yesterday recounting the
abduction of one Chen Hsi-chang on Nanking Road is untrue
because he had not gone to the Chocolate Shop but was
having a talking elsewhere with one of his friends.
page_data.zh:
1939年12月17日。晨间译文。

《中美日报》、《申报》、《新闻报》及
《国民新闻》:-

南京路发生政治绑架案

昨晚9时05分，南京路巧克力店门前发生了一起具有政治性质的绑架案，一名名为陈宪章 (陳憲章 ) 的人被强行带走，此人曾是本地新闻记者联谊会的职员。
据悉，名为袁肖逸 (Yuan Siao-yih (袁肖逸 ) )、别名袁学易 (Yuan Hsueh-yen (袁學易 ) ) 的人，系前魏龙社 (Wei Lung News Agency (魏龍社 ) ) 编辑，自向汪精卫派系投诚以来，一直企图在新闻界制造危害。然而，由于他与新闻界成员不太熟悉，他曾多次邀请陈宪章商议，希望诱使后者充当其线人，但每次均未成功。最近受到袁的逼迫，陈昨晚前往巧克力店，意在向袁阐明忠义之道。因担心发生意外麻烦，陈与几位朋友一同前往该地。到达该地时，陈注意到店前停着三辆私家车，其中两辆的车牌号为8021和4693。袁当时正站在其中一辆车旁。看到陈走近，他强行将陈塞进其中一辆车内，该车随后高速向西驶去，另两辆车紧随其后。据信他们驶向了西区方向。

《中美日报》及《新闻报》:-

南京路绑架报道据称不实

一名自称陈锡章 (Chen Hsi-chang (陈锡章 ) ) 的人通过电话告知本报，昨日各报刊登的关于陈宪章在南京路被绑架的报道不实，因为他并未去巧克力店，而是在别处与一位朋友谈话。

law under the name Chang Lih (張立). Between January
1938 and May 1939 he was concurrently member of the editorial
staff of the Standard (文匯報), 436 Foochow Road, which
made its first appearance in January 1938 but has never
resumed publication since its registration certificate was
withdrawn in May 1939, H.B.M. Ambassatorial certificate
being withdrawn shortly afterwards.

The Ping Ming News Agency is a reputable one and
supplies news to most of the leading Chinese dailies.
During its nearly one year of existence it has come to the
notice of the Police on only one occasion when it
satisfactorily explained what was at first thought to be an
exaggerated report on the assassination of a S.M.P.
superintendent.

参照所附上海英国大使馆新闻参赞办公室的来函，本处掌握有关平明通讯社（Ping Ming News Agency）的如下信息：

该社于1940年2月26日向本处申请注册，申报其编辑及印刷地址为爱德华七世路160号502室。注册业主、出版人及总编辑一直是张季涯（Chang Chi-yah），至今未变。这位先生约在1924年至1931年间担任本地主要中文日报《申报》（地址：汉口路309号）本地新闻栏目的编辑；约在1931年至1939年间，他以张立（Chang Lih）为名从事律师职业。1938年1月至1939年5月间，他兼任《文汇报》（Standard，地址：福州路436号）的编辑人员，该报于1938年1月首次出版，但自1939年5月注册证书被吊销后从未复刊，英王陛下大使证书也在不久后被吊销。

June 18, 1940. Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald, Ta Mei Pao, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Central China Daily News, Circulation Daily News :-

ASSASSINATION OF S.M.P. "C" DIVISION SUPERINTENDENT

At 8.15 a.m. yesterday a shooting took place at the tram stop at the corner of Avenue and Ferry Roads in which Liu Yung-kuei (劉永貴), Chinese Superintendent of the S.M.P. "C" Division, was shot and died on the spot. There were about ten gunmen, all of whom succeeded in making good their escape after committing the crime.

Superintendent Liu Yung-kuei alias Liu Yeu-ching (劉友卿), age 52, native of Wusih, resided at No.20 Vung Teh Faung (文德坊), corner of Avenue and Ferry Roads. Following the outbreak of the hostilities, he was transferred from "C" Division to Central Police Station. He was straight-forward and economical. At about 8.15 a.m. yesterday, the Superintendent, wearing uniform, left home on his way to office. He walked to the tram stop, there to wait for No.1 or No.2 Route tramcar. However, there were about ten outlaws lying in wait and, on seeing the Superintendent approaching, six of them went up and encircled the Superintendent, after which four of them, wearing white silk clothing, drew their pistols and fired. The Superintendent was taken completely by surprise and, before he was able to draw his service pistol, he was fatally struck by three bullets, one in the left temple, one in the right side of his neck and the third in his back. All three bullets lodged in his body. The Superintendent collapsed and died on the spot immediately. The gunmen, seeing their mission accomplished, took to flight and managed to make their escape before the arrival of the Police. A party of officers from Bubbling Well Police Station arrived on the scene to conduct an investigation and spent shells were collected for ballistic examination. The body of the murdered Superintendent was taken to the Police Hospital on Shanhaikwan Road and, after an inquest was held by a Court official in the afternoon, it was removed to the International Funeral Directors on Kiaochow Road. The body will be encoffined on the afternoon of June 19.

It is learned that the Police took a Cantonese maidservant (an eyewitness to the shooting) employed by the occupant of House No.24 Vung Teh Faung, to the police station for interrogation.

The late Superintendent had served with the S.M.P. for 38 years. He was loyal and diligent and was wholly relied upon by the authorities. After graduating from the middle school department of St. John's University at the age of 19, the late Mr. Liu joined the Clerical Staff of the S.M.P. on February 6, 1902, and was attached to Yangtsepoo Police Station, from which he was transferred 12 years later to Louza Police Station. After remaining at the latter police station for 6 years, he was transferred to the former Mixed Court as an interpreter. He was promoted to the rank of Superintendent on October 16, 1930 and had been attached to "A", "B" and "C" Divisions. He was impartial and courteous. It is said that the S.M.P. express deep regret over the untimely death of the late Superintendent and that steps are being discussed to bestow an exceptional posthumous reward.

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处长办公室 1940年6月18日）
1940年6月18日。晨间译稿

《中美日报》、《国民新闻报》、《大美报》、《申报》、《新闻晚报》、《华中日报》、《循环日报》：

工部局警务处“C”分区督察遇刺身亡

昨日上午8时15分，在爱文义路（Avenue Road）与斐伦路（Ferry Road）转角处的电车站发生枪击事件，工部局警务处“C”分区华籍督察刘永贵中弹，当场死亡。枪手约有十人，作案后均成功逃脱。

死者刘永贵，别名刘友卿，现年52岁，无锡人，居住于爱文义路与斐伦路转角处的文德坊20号。战事爆发后，他从“C”分区调至中央捕房。他为人直爽节俭。昨日上午8时15分左右，该督察身着制服离家前往办公室。他步行至电车站，等候1路或2路电车。然而，约有十名歹徒埋伏在此，见督察走近，其中六人上前将其包围，随后四名身穿白色丝绸服装的歹徒拔出手枪射击。督察完全措手不及，尚未及拔出佩枪，即被三发子弹击中致命，分别击中左太阳穴、颈部右侧及背部。三颗子弹均留在体内。督察倒地，当场立即死亡。枪手见任务完成，随即逃窜，并在警察到达前成功逃脱。静安寺捕房的一队警员抵达现场进行调查，并收集了弹壳以供弹道检验。遇害督察的遗体被送往山海关路警察医院，下午经法庭官员验尸后，移至胶州路万国殡仪馆。遗体将于6月19日下午入殓。

据悉，警方已将爱文义路文德坊24号住户雇用的一名广东籍女佣（枪击案目击者）带往捕房讯问。

已故督察在工部局警务处服务长达38年。他忠诚勤勉，深获当局信赖。已故刘先生19岁从圣约翰大学中学部毕业后，于1902年2月6日加入工部局警务处文书职员队伍，隶属于杨树浦捕房，12年后调至老闸捕房。在老闸捕房任职6年后，他被调往前混合法庭担任翻译。他于1930年10月16日晋升为督察职级，曾隶属于“A”、“B”和“C”分区。他公正且彬彬有礼。据悉，工部局警务处对已故督察的英年早逝深表遗憾，正讨论给予特殊的死后抚恤。

June 18, 1940.

The late Mr. Liu had some savings. He is
survived by six children, the eldest being a daughter named
Liu Soo-ya (劉素儀), aged 29, who is a graduate of the
Shanghai Law College with a B.A. degree and who is at present
practising law, with offices located in the downstairs left
wing of his house. She is married to Mr. Li Yuan-wei(李元義)
who is now studying abroad. The next is a son named Liu Bei-
li (劉培禮), aged 21, who is studying in the Senior Third
Year Class of the Kwang Zuh Middle School (光華中學). The
third is a daughter named Liu Sui-ya (劉瑞儀), age 17,
studying in the Senior First Year Class of the Bei Zung Middle
School for Girls (培成女中). The fourth and fifth are sons
named Liu Bei-chu (劉培初) and Liu Bei-sin (劉培信),
aged 14 and 12 respectively, studying in the Gonzaga College.
The youngest is a daughter named Liu Vung-ya (劉文儀), age 9,
studying in the Bei Zung Primary School ( ).

已故刘先生留有一些积蓄。他有六名子女幸存，长女名为刘素仪，29岁，毕业于上海法政学院，获文学士学位，目前从事律师职业，事务所位于其住宅楼下左翼。她嫁给了李元义先生，李先生目前正在国外留学。次子名为刘培礼，21岁，就读于光华中学高三年级。三女名为刘瑞仪，17岁，就读于培成女中高一年级。第四子和第五子分别为刘培初和刘培信，年龄分别为14岁和12岁，就读于震旦大学。幼女名为刘文仪，9岁，就读于培成小学（原文不清）。

Subject. Ping Ming News Agency - Application for Registration
Made by. D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Chang Chi-yah (張寄涯),
editor and manager of the Ping Ming News Agency
(平明通訊社), with an office in Room 502, House 160
Avenue Edward VII.
Chang Chi-yah, native of Shaoshing, age 53,
is at present unemployed. In 1928, he joined the
Shun Pao (申報), local leading Chinese daily, as
editor of the local news section, which post he held
up to the end of 1929. At the beginning of 1930,
he started to operate a firm known as the Ming Kwang
Bookstore (明光書店) situated at 104 Paoshan Road,
Chapei. Following the outbreak of hostilities in
1937, he returned to his native place. It was only
in February this year that he returned to this city.
The news agency in question which it is
proposed will commence functioning some time this
month will supply the local Press with material relating
to conditions in Shaoshing and local educational
and social news.

Subject Ni Feng Yuen Kan - Further objectionable matter published

Made by D. S. I. Young Forwarded by A. C. Mason

Reference instructions of D.C. (Special Branch)
appended to attached report of September 26, 1940, Li Leng-
chia (李蒙伽), editor, publisher and proprietor of the Ni
Feng Yuen Kan (藝風月刊), a monthly magazine in Chinese,
was called to and attended Headquarters on September 27
when he was informed that copies of one more issue (October
issue) must be submitted to this office for examination prior
to registration of his magazine being considered.

Up to December 24, 1940, no copies of the October
issue had been received by this office. On December 25, the
offices of the magazine were communicated with by telephone
enquiring about the Ni Feng Yuen Kan, and on December 28 the
attached copies of November and December issues were received.

Perusal shows that in the December issue is contained
a play entitled "A scene in the metropolis" which bears
dialogues such as "On the third week following the outbreak
of the August 13 hostilities when they escaped from Chapei,
the grandmother and the father of this little girl were
sacrificed under the severe bombings by the enemy ...."

It is suggested that editor be warned to be more
careful in the selection of words, and that Registration
Certificate be issued.

Bond?

A. C. (Special Branch).

主题 《艺风月刊》 - 再次刊登违禁内容

由副督察杨（Young）呈报，转呈自助理督察 A. C. Mason

参照特别课副警务处长在1940年9月26日附呈报告上的指示，中文月刊《艺风月刊》的编辑、出版人及业主李蒙伽于9月27日被召至总部，并被告知在其杂志注册申请被考虑之前，必须向本办公室提交下一期（十月刊）的样本。

截至1940年12月24日，本办公室未收到十月刊的样本。12月25日，通过电话与该杂志社联系，询问《艺风月刊》事宜，并于12月28日收到附呈的十一月和十二月刊样本。

经审阅发现，十二月刊中包含一出题为《都市一景》的剧本，其中有如下对白：“八月十三日战事爆发后的第三周，当他们从闸北逃出来时，这个小女孩的祖母和父亲在敌人的猛烈轰炸下牺牲了……”

建议警告编辑在选词上更加谨慎，并发放注册证书。

January 24, 1941 on the subject of a monthly magazine
called Ni Feng Yueh Kan (荔風月刊), enquiries show that

has also been ascertained from the employees of the

suggested that the attached certificate, which was made

been issued, be cancelled.

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for registration received from Chen Ping-shu (陳屏書), editor of the Siao Chieh Hua Pao (小姐畫報), a monthly magazine in Chinese, with offices at 380 Foochow Road.

Chen Ping-shu, native of Kiangyin, aged 24, came to Shanghai in February 1935, and entered the China Book Co. (中國書局雜誌公司), 380 Foochow Road, working as a member of the editorial staff of the firm. This post he held until October 1937 when he went into the employ of the Modern Art Co. (時代美術公司), 143 Avenue Edward VII, where he has occupied a similar post.

Li Poh-shing (李卜欣), the proprietor and publisher, native of Ningpo, aged 25, is at present an employee of the Accounting Department of the China Science Corporation, an American-owned firm at 649 Avenue Foch, which concern he joined in January 1937.

Nothing to the detriment of the applicants is known to this office.

The Siao Chieh Hua Pao made its first appearance in September 1935 and continued publication until September the following year when it had to suspend publication owing to poor circulation and shortage of funds. As necessary funds have now been raised by the proprietor, the Siao Chieh Hua Pao resumed publication on August 20, 1940 (copy attached). Subject Ta Dong Sin Koo Sien - Application for registration

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Chu Ying (朱嬰), editor
of the Ta Dong Sin Koo Sien (大同新歌選), a monthly
magazine containing screen songs in Chinese and
English, with offices at House 142 Moulmein Road.
Chu Ying, native of Soochow, aged 27, is at
present vocal broadcaster at the Hwa Ying Radio
Station (華英電台), 441 Hankow Road, which post he
has held since March 1939. He is also editor and
proprietor of the Selected Jazz Song Pocket-book
(爵士袖珍歌選), a non-periodical publication
registered with the S.M. Police under No.C. 810 (file
attached).
Yao Min (姚敏), the proprietor and publisher,
native of Shanghai, aged 24, was formerly employee
of the Chung Hwa Shipping Office (中華船業事務所), 10
Zung An Li (仁安里), Rue Baron Gros, which firm he
joined in July 1935 and left in December 1937 when it
closed down owing to losses sustained. He is at
present a member of the office staff of the Licence
Issuing Section of the S.M.C. which section he claims
to have joined in January 1938.
Nothing to the detriment of the applicants is
known to this office.
The first issue (attached) of this magazine
appeared on August 1, 1940. It carries love songs in
Chinese, foreign screen songs and advertisements of
commercial concerns, but nothing objectionable from

Subject Chih Sheh Wen Chai Yueh Kan - Application for registration -
Two issues examined
Made by D. S. I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Reference instructions of D.C. (Special Branch)
appended to attached report of September 9, 1940, Chin
Zung-feng (景仁芳), editor, publisher and proprietor
of the Chih Sheh Wen Chai Yueh Kan (知識文摘月刊),
a monthly magazine in Chinese, was called to Headquarters
on September 12, when he was informed that registration
would be considered by Police only after he had
submitted to this office copies of first two issues
of his magazine for examination.

The first issue appeared on October 10 and
the second issue on November 10, 1940. Perusal of
these two issues (attached) shows them to contain
reading matter on scientific knowledge, self-tuition,
technical knowledge, small industry, and current events
such as "Burma-Yunnan Communications" and the "Present
Situation in Philippines" and advertisements of
commercial concerns, but nothing objectionable from a
police point of view.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 1940）
A. G. (Special Branch).

D. S. I. Young

REPORT
Date Sept. 9, 1940.

Subject Chih Sheh Wen Chai Yueh Kan - Application for Registration

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Chin Zung-fang (景仁芳),
editor, publisher and proprietor of the Chih Sheh Wen
Chai Yueh Kan (知識文摘月刊), proposed monthly
magazine in Chinese, with offices at 34 Sinza Road.
Chin Zung-fang, native of Shaoshing, aged 23,
was formerly a clerk in the employ of lawyer Yao Chao-
li (姚兆里) with offices at 233 Nanking Road, which
post he held from July 1936 to December 1937. In
January 1938 he went into the employ of the Capital
Trading Co. (天一貿易公司), Room 603 House 113 Kiukiang
Road, where he has worked as secretary. He is also
editor of the Siao Kung Nye Semi-monthly (小工藝半月刊),
a Chinese language magazine, registered with the S.M.
Police under No.C. 355 (file attached). Nothing to
his detriment is known to this office.
The proposed magazine will contain articles
on the study of small industry in addition to the study
of science, self-tuition, geographical knowledge, etc.

(S.D.) REGISTRY
DATE 16/11/40

D. C. (Special Branch).

D. S. I.

Sin (寄影週讯), which was brought in by Hsu Yeh-kong

after the appearance of the 4th issue sometime in

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 5, Special Branch, Station,
REPORT
Date Oct. 29, 1940.
Subject Philosophy Monthly - Application for registration
Made by D.S. Pharazyn Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Zi Chih-ying (錢美),
editor, publisher and proprietor of the Philosophy
Monthly (哲学月刊), proposed magazine in Chinese,
with offices at House 21 Lane 238 Weihaiwei Road.
Zi Chih-ying, native of Quinsan, aged 22, came
to Shanghai in July 1936 and studied at the Shanghai
Middle School (上海中学), then located at 400 Rue
du Marche, where he graduated in June 1939. In July
the same year he entered the Chinan University
(暨南大学), 528 Connaught Road, and since then has
followed a course of philosophy. Nothing to his
detriment is known to this office.
The proposed magazine will contain translations
of articles on philosophy reproduced from western
publications and matter on the characteristics of the
historical philosophy in China.

D. S.
D. C. (Crime and Special Branches).

(上海文显), a monthly magazine in Chinese, dated Sept. 15, 1940.

Page 12

The women digging potatoes immediately threw away
their implements, hoping to pass unnoticed by enemy planes.
But the Nazi bombers were not satisfied, and soon they returned
and raked the field with a volley of machine-gun fire, as
a result of which two women were killed.

Page 15

While standing in the garden at the American Embassy,
I witnessed personally a German bomber shot down by anti-aircraft.
I was just ready with my camera and got the picture when that
cruel plane descended in flames.

In celebrating the fall of that cruel plane, we had
forgotten the families of those fliers back in Germany who
were in a state of great anxiety about them. We knew that
they represented the German Government and for the past three
weeks had in cold-blooded heartlessness killed people. It
is not unfair that the war has done this to them.

1940年9月15日出版的中文月刊《上海文显》（Shang Hai Wen Sien）第一期校样中出现的“华沙围城战”一文摘录译文。

第12页

正在挖土豆的妇女们立即扔下工具，希望不被敌机发现。
但纳粹轰炸机并不满足，很快又返回，用一阵机枪扫射田地，
导致两名妇女死亡。

第15页

站在美国大使馆的花园里时，
我亲眼目睹一架德国轰炸机被高射炮击落。
当那架残酷的飞机带着火焰坠落时，我刚准备好相机并拍下了照片。

在庆祝那架残酷飞机的坠毁时，我们
忘记了那些飞行员在德国的家人，他们正为他们处于极度焦虑之中。我们知道，
他们代表德国政府，在过去三周里，以冷酷无情的心肠杀害人民。
战争对他们做出这种事，并非不公。

「天工開物」之書，雖非專為陶瓷而作，然其中所載製瓷之法，實為研究中國陶瓷史之重要文獻。宋應星於明末所著此書，不僅記錄了當時之工藝技術，更反映了社會經濟與文化背景。其內容涵蓋農業、手工業等多個領域，對後世影響深遠。

「景德镇陶录」乃清代藍浦所撰，系統總結了景德鎮瓷器生產經驗。該書詳細描述了從原料選取到成品燒成之全过程，並附有圖示說明。對於理解傳統制瓷工藝具有極高價值。此外，书中還提及各地窯口特色及市場需求變化，是研究古代陶瓷貿易的重要資料。

關於「龍泉青瓷」的研究，近年來取得顯著進展。通過考古發掘與科學分析，學者們揭示了龍泉窯在不同歷史時期的發展脈絡及其獨特風格形成原因。特別是對釉色變化的探討，有助於我們更好地欣賞這一世界級非物質文化遺產的魅力所在。

至於「汝官哥定鈞」五大名窯之間關係問題，歷來爭論不休。有人認為它們各自獨立發展；也有人主張存在相互借鑒現象。無論如何，這些窯場共同構成了宋代瓷器藝術輝煌篇章，值得深入挖掘與保護傳承下去。

最後需要強調的是，在進行相關研究時必須注重實地考察與文獻相結合的方法論原則。只有這樣才能確保結論準確可靠，避免主觀臆斷或片面解讀帶來的誤差。希望未來能有更多優秀成果問世，推動我國陶瓷學科建設不斷向前邁進！

世界週刊之迴響
張安樂譯
The Times Weekly Edition

在現代世界中，我們對於「自由」一詞的意義，往往感到困惑。它是一個被用的字眼，一個被政治家和宣傳家們用來掩飾其真實意圖的工具。然而，真正的自由並非僅僅是擺脫外在的束縛，而是內在的解放——從恐懼、偏見和無知中解放出來。只有當一個人能夠独立思考，不受外界壓力的影響，他才能真正稱得上是自由的。這種自由需要勇氣和智慧，需要對真理的追求和對正義的堅持。在當今這個充滿挑戰的時代，我們更需要這樣的自由精神，來面對未來的不確定性。

回顧歷史，我們可以看到，許多偉大的思想家都曾為自由而奮鬥。他們用自己的生命和心血，換來了後人的自由與尊嚴。然而，自由並不是一勞永逸的，它需要每一代人不斷地去爭取和維護。在當前的社會中，我們面臨著新的挑戰：科技的發展帶來了便利，但也帶來了新的監控和控制手段；全球化的進程促進了交流，但也加劇了文化衝突和身份認同的危機。在這樣的背景下，我們如何保持自己的獨立性和自主性，成為了一個亟待解決的問題。

此外，自由還意味著責任。一個真正自由的人，不僅要對自己負責，也要對他人和社會負責。他不能因為追求個人的利益而損害他人的權益，也不能因為逃避責任而放棄自己的權利。自由與責任是相輔相成的，只有在承擔起相應的責任之後，我們才能真正享受到自由的樂趣。因此，我們在追求自由的同時，也應該時刻提醒自己，不要忘記自己所肩負的責任。

最後，我想說的是，自由是一種狀態，更是一種態度。它不是別人賜予的，而是自己爭取來的。只有當我們內心充滿了對自由的渴望，並且願意為此付出努力時，我們才能真正擁有自由。讓我們一起努力，為了那個更加美好、更加自由的未來而奮鬥吧！

今天面對氣候變遷和生態破壞的挑戰，我們必須正視海洋所面臨的危機。數十年來，人類對海洋的
無止盡索取，已使海洋生態系統岌岌可危。大堡礁白化、北極海冰融化、過度捕撈等問題，都顯示出
海洋正面臨前所未有的危機。「我們不能再忽視這個問題了。」一位海洋生物學家警告道。他指出，
如果我們不採取行動，未來的世代將無法享受到海洋的美好。「我們必須現在就行動起來，保護我們
的海洋。」他說。這不僅是為了海洋生物，也是為了人類自己。海洋提供了我們食物、氧氣和氣候調
節等功能。如果海洋崩潰，人類也將無法倖免。「我們必須改變我們的行為，減少污染和過度捕撈，
並建立更多的海洋保護區。」他強調。「這是我們對未來世代的責任。」

然而，許多人仍然對此漠不關心。他們認為海洋問題離他們很遠，或者認為個人的力量微不足道。
但事實上，每個人的行為都會對海洋產生影響。減少使用塑膠製品、支持永續漁業、參與海灘清潔活
動等，都是我們可以做的事情。「不要小看個人的力量，」一位環保活動家說。「每個人的努力匯聚起
來，就能產生巨大的改變。」她呼籲大家從日常生活做起，為保護海洋貢獻一份心力。「讓我們一起努
力，讓海洋恢復生機，讓未來的世代也能享受到海洋的美好。」 （選自天下雜誌 第 700 期）

瑞典不朽詩人斯特林堡於一九一二年五月十四日在斯德哥爾摩逝世，享年六十三歲。他生前曾寫過許多劇本和小說，其中最有名的是《朱麗小姐》和《父親》等作品。他的戲劇風格獨特，充滿心理分析與社會批判色彩，對後世影響深遠。Roll Out the Barrel 是他晚年創作的一部重要劇作，描寫了一個家庭內部矛盾衝突的故事。該劇通過細膩的人物刻畫和緊張的情節發展，展現了人性中的複雜面以及社會環境對個人命運的影響。此外，他还创作了大量的散文、诗歌和其他文学作品，为瑞典文学的发展做出了巨大贡献。

去年年底十二月中旬時分左右，有一位名叫李明的年輕人來到北京旅遊觀光。他在遊覽故宮博物院期間偶然發現了一件非常珍貴的历史文物——一件明代青花瓷瓶。这件瓷器不仅工艺精湛而且保存完好无损因此引起了专家们的高度关注经过鉴定确认其确系真品后决定将其收藏于国家博物馆内供公众欣赏研究之用同时也标志着我国古代陶瓷艺术成就得到了进一步肯定与弘扬发扬光大之目的得以实现矣！

「而從這個神，在德國非常地被人敬三口崇拜。他有一「極好名字」……「光輝、榮耀與令人敬畏的名字——一換小孩子說！米拉只！這新詞彙，縱橫，他配行足跡所及處」。木匠般壯觀。布達佩斯說：「我生之效。奧斯陸人十四世紀時。其根悠久。大數歸一正當的應用。」

問！那提制，也難免太強大了一點。因此，我們應該先仔細且審慎地評估其用途！我深信它。在故鄉的田園之中。我配成什麼呢！請記住你永遠是快樂。人們必將羨慕了。竟未發現像這樣大而堅固的。我配最大者……城堡莊園。相信我能作深遠的用途吧。你聽我配說罷。他配存在即代表著無限可能與未來之光。並非三次「因緣際會來會場出席這種會議一」我配卡大筆法文中。並且我配……「世間萬物皆有定數啊～！」我配配回了一笑……「你配說得對。我配的確是個了不起的家。我配配能如此了。

誰說。世上人皆難逃命運安排——一切都無法避免注定的發生。這是無可奈何的事實。天意不可違。既然已分九十九千五十五個數據型人，你就放寬心吧。你若已天意決。就該接受現實。我已憶起往事歷歷在目「我錯」了十七年。也許當時我十分無知(Scandinavia)等四十幾個地區被佔。一一滅亡。這世界缺乏人情味。實在冷酷無情令人寒心。何能奢望仁慈與和平共存下去呢？

特隆赫姆(Trondheim)——北歐挪威大城市之一。位於挪威中部海岸中心地——諾爾蘭郡境內。在維京時代，此乃重要貿易港口(Husnes)附近。據說這裡曾是國王宮殿所在地！並設市。然目前僅存古蹟遺址。市容破舊！繁華不再。雖然當地政府試圖恢復往日風貌女扮男裝。期許能在短期內完成重建工作。無奈資金短缺。

（47）
（選自《中國古代戰爭史》）

西歐戰場的巡視
杜聿明

余於民國三十四年春，奉命赴歐洲戰場考察。此行目的，在觀察盟軍作戰之實際情況，以供我軍參考。余自重慶出發，經印度、埃及、義大利，最後抵達法國。沿途所見，深感盟軍裝備之精良，訓練之嚴謹，指揮之靈活，實非我軍所能及。然盟軍亦有其弱點，如後勤補給之困難，士兵士氣之低落等。余以為，我軍應吸取盟軍之長處，避免其短處，以期在未來之戰爭中，取得勝利。

余在歐洲戰場，曾參觀多次戰役。其中印象最深者，為諾曼第登陸戰。此戰役中，盟軍以海空優勢，成功登陸法國海岸，並迅速推進。德軍雖頑強抵抗，但終因兵力懸殊，而告失敗。余以為，此戰役之勝利，主要在於盟軍之海空優勢，以及後勤補給之充足。我軍若欲在未來之戰爭中取得勝利，必須加強海空力量，並確保後勤補給之充足。

余又曾參觀義大利戰場。此戰場中，盟軍與德軍在山區進行激烈戰鬥。德軍利用地形優勢，頑強抵抗，使盟軍進展緩慢。余以為，此戰場之經驗，對我軍極具參考價值。我軍應學習德軍利用地形優勢之方法，並在未來之戰爭中，善用地形，以取得勝利。

余在歐洲戰場，亦曾參觀蘇聯紅軍之作戰。紅軍之裝備，雖不如盟軍精良，但其士兵之勇猛，指揮之果斷，實令人敬佩。余以為，我軍應學習紅軍之精神，並在未來之戰爭中，發揚此种精神，以取得勝利。

余此次歐洲之行，收穫頗豐。余將把所見所聞，整理成報告，呈報上級，以供參考。余希望，我軍能從中吸取教訓，並在未來之戰爭中，取得勝利。

（48）

劉三復方鎮推轂許曹鬆等。愈與公大抵皆非能終交久處者故也予安可大哉五嶺外非所□□之人。數後必
由斯出且繼茲數十百歲名士不少德乃在其中爾後。然經回民！輕近十人。余始任職口食反艱拙。仕宦清
難堪物業！雖兼校。可免憂惶囈囈終能活罷休矣。

擬賀侍郎啟陸人。正在正議事中。聽訟受味。禁北余，家禁子一限。罪難禁治江蘇民五十人，兩族
權在求恩。瞻望水館。慰云新出而獲其裁。所荷恩力分大。何足一報。出觀囑託察臣察計居然下部。竊
王畿區回斷。當此巨任。然竊聞能保效王之節義及有風。無失本业。恐草信從之徒「既安之亦難。」

戰爭之勝負，視於其後方之能力。國家之安全與繁榮，亦視其經濟之強弱。故戰時之經濟，尤爲重要。已見諸報章雜誌者，多矣。茲將其中要點錄出，以供參考。

一、德國之工業，雖經戰火摧殘，然其基礎尚存。其鋼鐵、化學、電氣等工業，仍具相當實力。且其技術人員，多未損失，故恢復甚速。

二、德國之農業，雖受戰爭影響，然其生產力仍高。其糧食自給率，約達百分之八十。且其農產品之品質，亦佳。

三、德國之交通，雖遭破壞，然其鐵路、公路、水運等，仍能維持基本運輸。且其運輸效率，亦高。

四、德國之財政，雖因戰爭而困難，然其稅收、公債等，仍能維持基本開支。且其金融體系，亦穩健。

五、德國之外貿，雖受戰爭限制，然其進出口貿易，仍能維持基本平衡。且其外匯儲備，亦充足。

六、德國之勞動力，雖因戰爭而減少，然其勞動生產率，仍高。且其勞工素質，亦佳。

七、德國之科技，雖因戰爭而受阻，然其科研機構，仍能維持基本運作。且其科技成果，亦豐。

八、德國之教育，雖因戰爭而受影響，然其教育體系，仍能維持基本運作。且其教育質量，亦高。

九、德國之醫療，雖因戰爭而受影響，然其醫療體系，仍能維持基本運作。且其醫療水平，亦高。

十、德國之社會保障，雖因戰爭而受影響，然其社會保障體系，仍能維持基本運作。且其社會保障水平，亦高。

然而，由於內部政治分歧嚴重，加上經濟困難重重，使得新政府在處理內外事務時面臨巨大挑戰。特別是關於如何重建軍隊、恢復生產以及穩定社會秩序等問題，都需要妥善解決才能確保國家長遠發展。

以上所述。僅就英德兩國海軍競賽之概況而言。若詳加分析。則可見其中種種複雜因素。例如地理環境、經濟實力、政治制度、外交政策等。皆對海軍發展有重大影響。茲分述如下：

一、地理環境：英國為島國。四面環海。賴海運以維持生命。故必須保持強大之海軍。以保護其貿易路線及殖民地。德國則位於歐洲大陸。陸上強敵環伺。故其軍事重點在陸軍。海軍僅為輔助。然威廉二世好大喜功。欲使德國成為世界強國。乃大力擴充海軍。此與其地理環境不符。故終致失敗。

二、經濟實力：英國為工業革命發源地。經濟實力雄厚。足以支撐龐大海軍。德國雖亦工業發達。但起步較晚。且資源有限。難以長期與英國競爭。故其海軍擴張計劃。實超出其經濟負荷能力。

三、政治制度：英國為君主立憲國。議會權力強大。政府決策須經議會批准。故海軍擴張計劃較為穩健。德國為君主專制國。皇帝權力至高無上。議會形同虛設。故威廉二世可獨斷獨行。推行其冒險之海軍政策。

四、外交政策：英國奉行「光榮孤立」政策。不與任何國家結盟。以保持行動自由。德國則企圖打破此種局面。建立同盟體系。以對抗英國。然其外交手段拙劣。反使自己陷入孤立。終致失敗。

綜上所述。英德海軍競賽之失敗。實由多種因素造成。非單一原因所致。吾人當引以為戒。避免重蹈覆轍。

（78）

最後。吾人應注意者。海軍競賽不僅耗費巨資。且易引發戰爭。故各國應本和平共處之精神。通過談判解決爭端。而非訴諸武力。唯有如此。方能確保世界和平與繁榮。否則。歷史悲劇必將重演。人類文明亦將遭受嚴重打擊。此誠吾人所當警惕者也。

【法 Scharnhorst 將軍】。普魯士改革派軍事領袖。十九世紀初【普魯士改革】之核心人物。推動廢除農奴制、建立義務兵役制、改革參謀本部等現代化軍事制度。其思想深刻影響後世德國乃至世界軍事發展。

普魯士在耶拿戰役中慘敗於拿破崙，國土淪喪，軍隊潰散。為挽救國家危亡，沙恩霍斯特等人發起軍事改革。他主張建立普遍義務兵役制，取代舊有的僱兵與貴族軍官體系；設立戰爭部與總參謀部，實現軍事指揮專業化；創辦柏林軍事學院，培養新型軍官人才。這些措施使普魯士軍隊脫胎換骨，成為日後統一德意志的武力基礎。

沙恩霍斯特不僅是軍事改革家，亦是民族主義者。他認為軍隊應屬於國家而非君主個人，強調公民責任與愛國精神。他在萊比錫會戰前病逝，未能親見普魯士最終勝利，但其理念由格奈森瑙等人繼承發揚。他的改革被視為近代軍事體制之觴，對歐洲各國產生深遠影響。（18）

遵旨查办外。因查该处地民贫，向无出产堪资生计者。
并据该府县禀称，前因灾歉频仍，民多流亡，现虽渐次复业，而元气未复，
尚需抚恤。臣等查该处情形，实与别处不同，若照例办理，恐不足以示体恤。
拟请特恩，将该处钱粮蠲免一年，以苏民困。伏乞皇上圣鉴训示。
谨奏。

奉朱批：知道了。钦此。

再，查该处被灾较重，民情困苦，非寻常赈济所能救济。臣等公同商酌，
拟请于该处设立粥厂，每日施粥，以救饥民。其经费由臣等捐廉凑办，
不另动支公款。是否有当，伏候圣裁。

又，查该处水利失修，田亩荒芜，若不急为整理，恐后患无穷。臣等拟
派员前往勘估，择要兴修，以期永赖。所需工料银两，另行筹拨。
合并陈明。

（印：军机处章）

（三）核议奏案

查原奏内称，该处被灾情形，已据该府县详细禀报，自应照例办理。
惟念该处民困已极，若拘泥成例，恐不足以拯危亡。臣等悉心核议，
拟请将该处钱粮全行蠲免，并加赈一个月，以广皇仁。
至设立粥厂一节，亦属可行，应即饬令该地方官妥为经理，毋得虚应故事。
其水利一事，关系民生甚大，应即派员勘估，速为兴修，以慰民望。
所有核议缘由，理合恭折具奏，伏乞皇上圣鉴。
谨奏。

（89）

不可謂是進步解放。此種之見解，原係由歐洲社會學輸入。惟今日世界潮流所趨已非昔日可比擬矣。
故吾人對於此種學說當加以研究。然亦須注意其流弊耳。

現在吾國社會組織尚屬舊式家庭制度為多。將來若欲改革則必先從教育入手。蓋教育乃根本大計也。且現今學校中所授知識多半偏重理論而少實際應用。以致學生畢業後往往不能適應社會需要。此實一大憾事也。

至於女子教育問題更應特別重視。因女性佔人口半數以上。倘不使其受良好教育則國家前途堪憂矣。況且現代文明各國皆以男女平等為原則。吾國豈可落人之後哉？

總而言之：欲求社會進步必須先改良教育制度。否則雖有良法美意終難收效也。

（91）

近來各地風氣漸開。青年男女紛紛要求自由戀愛結婚。此固屬可喜現象。但亦不可過於放任自流。以免發生不良後果。蓋婚姻大事關係終身幸福。不宜輕率從事也。

又聞某地有未婚先孕之事傳出。舆论譁然。家長們尤爲憤慨。認爲此等行爲敗壞風俗道德。宜嚴加懲處云云。其實此事責任不在當事人一方。社會環境與家庭教育亦有不可推卸之責焉。

試問今日之青少年何以如此膽大妄為？無非受外界誘惑太深所致耳。報紙雜誌電影戲劇等等无不宣揚情愛至上主義。使年輕人誤以為只要兩相情願便可任意結合。殊不知其中隱藏著許多危險陷阱等待著他們去跳入呢！

因此我們呼籲各界人士共同努力營造一個健康向上的文化氛圍。讓下一代能夠在正確價值觀引導下成長發展。唯有這樣才能真正實現民族復興偉業目標啊！

最後還要提醒各位讀者朋友們注意身體保健工作的重要性。畢竟健康才是革命本錢嘛！希望大家都能養成良好生活習慣並堅持鍛煉身體哦～祝願大家每天都充滿活力快樂每一天！！

調後的話

一九三三年九月一日，在芝加哥舉行之世界博覽會開幕日，已故之愛因斯坦博士曾以「科學與宗教」為題發表演說。他說：「科學沒有宗教是跛足的，宗教沒有科學是盲目的。」這句話，至今仍被視為科學與宗教關係的最佳註腳。然而，在這兩者之間，是否真的存在著不可逾越的鴻溝？或者，它們只是人類認識世界的兩種不同方式？

大哲學家康德（Immanuel Kant）曾說：「有兩樣東西，我們愈經常愈持久地加以思索，它們就愈使心靈充滿日新月異的景仰和敬畏：在我之上的星空和居我心中的道德法則。」這兩樣東西，一個是外在的自然界，一個是內在的精神世界。科學探索前者，宗教關懷後者。它們看似對立，實則互補。

在二十世紀中葉，物理學家海森堡（Werner Heisenberg）提出了著名的「不確定性原理」，指出我們無法同時精確測量粒子的位置和動量。這一發現不僅改變了我們對微觀世界的理解，也挑戰了傳統的决定論觀點。它暗示著，宇宙的本質或許並非完全可預測，而是包含著某種程度的隨機性和不确定性。這與某些宗教哲學中關於自由意志和神意安排的討論不謀而合。

另一方面，生物學家達爾文（Charles Darwin）的進化論揭示了生命形式的多樣性和複雜性是如何通過自然選擇逐漸形成的。這一理論雖然最初引發了巨大的爭議，但如今已被廣泛接受為解釋生物多樣性的基礎框架。然而，即使在接受進化論的前提下，許多科學家仍然認為，生命的起源和意識的本质等问题，仍需借助哲學或宗教的思考來尋求更深層次的理解。

當代著名物理學家霍金（Stephen Hawking）在其著作《時間簡史》中探討了宇宙的起源和結構。他提出，宇宙可能是一個自足的系统，不需要外部創造者的介入就能存在和发展。然而，他也承認，科學目前尚無法回答所有問題，特別是那些涉及價值、意義和目的的问题。這些問題往往屬於宗教和哲學的範疇。

總之，科學與宗教之間的關係並非簡單的對立或統一，而是一種動態的互動過程。它們各自提供了不同的視角和方法來探索真理，並在不斷對話和交流中豐富和完善人類的知識體系。正如愛因斯坦所言，科學與宗教應當相互尊重、相互借鑑，共同促進人類文明的进步与发展。

（本文作者系某大學哲學系教授，專研科學哲學與宗教哲學。）

Subject Shang Hai Wen Hien - application for registration

Made by. L.J. Pharazyn Forwarded by. W.H.T. Lawson

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Yeh Sin-an (叶心安),
editor and publisher of the Shang Hai Wen Hien
(上海文獻), proposed monthly magazine in Chinese,
with offices at 4 Lane 394 Foochow Road.
Yeh Sin-an, native of Kiangsu, age 31, is
also known as Yeh Hung-chao (叶洪超). He was
formerly chief of the Employment Section of the World's
Chinese Students Federation, 101 Carter Road, which
post he held between 1929 and 1935. In the
beginning of 1936 he joined the Chung Hwa Book Co.
(中華書局), 221 Honan Road, and undertook the post of
chief secretary until the spring of 1938 when he
became teacher of the Shanghai Middle School for Girls
(上海女中), 451 Taku Road. Commencing from 1939
he was taken on as a member of the staff of the China
Book Co. (中國什誌公司), 380 Foochow Road, which
post he still holds. He is at present concurrently
editor and publisher of the Tsing Nien Zin Kan
(青年旬刊), a ten-day magazine in Chinese registered
with the S.M.C. under No.C. 648, and editor of the
Chih Yeh Yu Shui Yang (職業與修養), a semi-monthly
magazine in Chinese registered under No.C. 551. He
was also editor and publisher of the Chi Wen News
Agency (集聞通訊社) for which certificate No.C. 548
was declared "null and void" by the Police on August 7,
1939 (file attached).

现随文转呈一份来自叶心安（Yeh Sin-an）的注册申请，叶氏系拟出版的中文月刊《上海文献》（Shang Hai Wen Hien）的编辑兼出版人，社址位于福州路394弄4号。
叶心安，江苏人，31岁，又名叶洪超（Yeh Hung-chao）。他曾任世界中国学生联合会（World's Chinese Students Federation，地址卡特路101号）就业部主任，该职任职时间为1929年至1935年间。1936年初，他加入河南路221号的中华书局（Chung Hwa Book Co.），担任总秘书一职，直至1938年春，他成为大沽路451号上海女中（Shanghai Middle School for Girls）的教师。自1939年起，他被福州路380号的中国什誌公司（China Book Co.）聘为职员，该职位目前仍在任。他目前还兼任在工部局注册号为C. 648的中文旬刊《青年旬刊》（Tsing Nien Zin Kan）的编辑兼出版人，以及注册号为C. 551的中文半月刊《职业与修养》（Chih Yeh Yu Shui Yang）的编辑。他还曾担任集闻通讯社（Chi Wen News Agency）的编辑兼出版人，该社证书编号C. 548已于1939年8月7日被警方宣布“无效”（附件存档）。

REPORT
Subject Ying Wu - Application for registration - First two issues examined
Made by. D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Reference instructions of P.A. to A.C. (Special Branch) appended to attached report of November 7, 1940, Chao Tien-pei (赵天悲), editor, publisher and proprietor of the Ying Wu (影舞), a weekly magazine in Chinese, was called to and attended Headquarters on November 9 when he was informed that copies of first two issues must be first submitted to this office for examination prior to registration being granted by the Police and warned that unless objectionable matter such as appeared in the Lieh Pao (力报), a mosquito paper in Chinese, registered with the S.M. Police under No.C. 50, was avoided, no registration would be effected. He promised to exercise due care in running his paper.

The first issue appeared on November 16 and the second issue on November 23, 1940. Perusal shows them to contain news and reports relating to cabarets and taxi-dancers, poems and pictures of taxi-dancers and advertisements of cabarets, but nothing objectionable from a police point of view.

A. C. (Special Branch).
D. S. I.

Forwarded herewith is an application for

editor, publisher and proprietor of the Ying Wu
(影舞), proposed weekly magazine in Chinese, with
offices at House 3 Lane 330 Yu Ya Ching Road.

Chao Tien-pei, native of Chekiang, aged 24,
is reporter on dancing news in the employ of the Lieh
Pao (力报), a mosquito daily paper, House 3 Lane
330 Yu Ya Ching Road, registered with the S.M. Police
under No.C. 50, which press he joined in 1938. He

赵天悲，浙江籍，24岁，受雇于《力报》，担任舞蹈新闻记者。《力报》是一家“蚊子报”（小型日报），社址位于愚园路330弄3号，已在上海公共租界警务处以C. 50号注册。他于1938年加入该报社。他同时兼任“银都舞厅”的广告经理，该舞厅位于福煦路988号，成立于1940年10月。本处未掌握任何对其不利的信息。

Strike - The China Press Workmen.

Since the initial report of this case was forwarded
the workers of the China Press, 160 Avenue Edward VII
have consented to return to work on the evening of
29-8-41 on condition that the management continue to
negotiate with them in connection with the previous
demands made on 25-8-41, this the management have
consented to do.

（批：S / [签名] / 30/8）

It was further ascertained that the management had
dismissed five of these employees who were believed to be
cause of the unrest, this resulted in the workers refusing
to return to work until such time as the five men were
re-instated, the management agreed to this demand but
refused to consider the other demands unless the men
immediately return to work, this has resulted in the men
returning to work while the other demands are being
negotiated between the Management, the workers and the
S.M.C. Industrial Section.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / AUG 1941 / ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER / SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：[签名] / 30/8）

At present these negotiations are deadlocked but the
management has stated that an early settlement is
expected as he is willing to grant them some consideration
but not on scale as demanded by the workers.

D.D.C. [签名]

（批：S. [签名]）

Reg. Rpt.

（左下角批注：Copy to Special Branch）

罢工 - 《大陆报》工人。

自本案初报发出以来，
位于爱德华七世路160号的《大陆报》工人
已同意于1941年8月29日晚复工，条件是资方继续
就其于1941年8月25日先前提出的要求与他们进行谈判，资方已同意这样做。

（批注：S / [签名] / 8月30日）

此外获悉，资方已解雇了五名被认为
是引起动荡原因的雇员，这导致工人拒绝
复工，直到这五人复职为止，资方同意了这一要求，但
拒绝考虑其他要求，除非工人立即
复工，这导致工人在资方、工人和
工部局工业科之间就其他要求进行谈判期间
返回工作岗位。

（印：上海公共租界工部局 / 1941年8月 / 助理处长 / 特务科）
（批注：[签名] / 8月30日）

目前这些谈判陷入僵局，但
资方表示预计会早日解决，因为他愿意给予他们一定的照顾，
但不会按照工人要求的规模。

STRIKE OF EMPLOYEES OF CHINA PRESS,160
AVENUE EDWARD VII.
---------------------------------------

At 1 a.m. 26/8/41 a telephone message was
received from Mr.Noo Kya Teng,manager of the China
Press,160 Av.Ed.VII,reporting that all type se□ers

some trouble was expected.

C.D.S. 118,C.D.C. 101 and the undersigned
attended and saw the above manager when it was
ascertained that about one week previously some
discontent was noticed among the workers of the above
newspaper and on enquiries being made by the manager
it was discovered that the workers were dissatisfied
with their salary,however as no demands were made
the management did not attempt to remedy the matter
as these workers' wages are based on a similarity

At about 9p.m. 25/8/41 these workers refused to
carry on with their work with the result that the
printing of the newspaper was delayed,the manager
talked with the workers which resulted in the following
demands being made:-

(1) That the workers basic salary be increased

爱多亚路160号《字林西报》（China Press）雇员罢工
---------------------------------------

1941年8月26日凌晨1时，接到爱多亚路160号《字林西报》经理Noo Kya Teng先生电话报告，称所有排字工和印刷工（约72人）正在罢工，预计会发生一些骚乱。

刑事侦缉处第118号警员、刑事侦缉处第101号警员及本人前往现场，会见了上述经理。经查明，大约一周前，该报社工人中已出现不满情绪；经理进行调查后发现，工人们对其薪水表示不满。然而，由于工人并未提出具体要求，管理层未试图解决此事，因为这些工人的工资标准与其他外文报纸雇员的工资标准相似。

1941年8月25日晚9时许，这些工人拒绝继续工作，导致报纸印刷延误。经理与工人交谈，结果工人提出了以下要求：

(1) 工人基本工资每月增加10元。
(2) 农历新年发放100元奖金。

（印：索引编制者

日期 1941年8月26日）

Italian Fascist Chief, Aides
Convicted For Leonof Assault

Giulio Costantini, Secretary of
the Italian Fascist Party here and
member of the S.M.C. Library
Committee, received a sentence
of 30 days in jail, transmuted
into a fine of 1,500 Lira,
when he and three other
Italians were found guilty in
the Italian Consular Court yes-
terday of assaulting Mr. George
Leonof, city editor of THE CHINA
PRESS. The sentence was
suspended by Judge R. Rapex
for five years.

Fennucci, secretary to the Press
Attache of the Italian Embassy,
and Morelli, a physical culture in-
structor, each received a sentence of
15 days' imprisonment, transmuted
into a fine of 750 Lira. Their
sentences were not suspended as
they had received previous convic-
tions in Shanghai. Corigliani, pro-
prietor of the La Moda tailor shop
on Avenue du Roi Albert, opposite
the Hai Alai Auditorium, received
the same sentence, suspended for
five years.

The Italians admitted attack-
ing Mr. Leonof on Friday, May
23. Fennucci, Corigliani and
Morelli said they had tried to
administer a bottle of castor-oil
to the newspaperman "because
we had been ordered to do so by
our leader, the Secretary of the
Fascist Party." Costantini ad-
mitted giving the order, and de-
clared he would "do so again if
it becomes necessary, and the
order will again be carried out."

Giving a passionate speech in
which he gesticulated, raised his
voice and was time and again told
by Judge R. Rapex to confine him-
self to relevant issues, Costantini
 inveighed against the "Democratic
so-called freedom of the press,
which is actually freedom to insult."
He said that in Shanghai "one acts
according to the weapons one has."
In a few months' time, he said
dryly, "we will perhaps have more
weapons."

"Symbolical Gesture"

Costantini declared that the at-
tack on Mr. Leonof by Fascist of-
ficials was not a dishonorable act.
The administration of castor-oil, he
explained, was a "symbolical gesture"
in reply to the articles which ap-
peared in THE CHINA PRESS. The
attack was not motivated by any
personal feeling against Mr. Leonof,
he added.

"We call Shanghai an interna-
tional city!" he exclaimed. "It is
an international impostor as Italian
interests help to patrol the streets.
The reality is: In Shanghai we
have British Jews, like Sassoon,
and Russian interests who think
only of their own interests..."

Costantini cited the
alleged anti-Italian articles in
THE CHINA PRESS and a cartoon
which he said had once appeared in
the Shanghai Evening Post and
Mercury, depicting the Japanese
Emperor pulling a cart. "Yet!" he
exclaimed, "when the Japanese pro-
tested to the Shanghai Municipal
Council, the Council said it could
do nothing because there is freedom
of the press in the Settlement!

His 'Light Jokes'

"Freedom of the press! It is
freedom of insult!" And he again
plunged into rhetorical dissertation
in which he mentioned Mussolini,
flung an arm dramatically at the
Judge, was again told by the latter
not to wander off the point, and
spoke scathingly of the "light jokes"
in the "Off the Record" column of
THE CHINA PRESS.

Mr. Leonof acted as his own
counsel. He explained that the
writing of editorials was outside his
province; and that he therefore was
not responsible for the editorial to
which the Italians had taken ex-
ception. He also pointed out that
management of a newspaper, and
not its employees, takes the respon-
sibility for what appears in it.

The facts of the incident, as re-
ported previously in the press, were
read out by Judge Rapex, telling
how the Italians had lured Mr.
Leonof to a vacant plot behind the
Italian Club on Great Western
Road, had there tried to make him
drink a bottle of castor oil, and
had assaulted him when he refused
to accede to their order.

Leonof Questions Costantini

Costantini denied any intention of
causing Mr. Leonof bodily harm.
They had merely wanted to make
him drink the castor oil, he ex-
plained. "And had I turned around
and walked away," Mr. Leonof
asked him, "would you have used
force?" Costantini admitted that
they would.

He then said he had been sure
Mr. Leonof had written the editorial
in question, as he had known that
he also wrote in the "Off the
Record" column. "Do you admit the
possibility of one man writing Off
Record and editorials?" Mr. Leonof
asked him. Costantini replied in the
affirmative.

意大利法西斯头目及其助手
因袭击Leonof被判刑

此处意大利法西斯党书记、工部局图书馆委员会委员Giulio Costantini，在与另外三名意大利人于昨日在意国领事法庭被裁定袭击《字林西报》本市版编辑George Leonof先生罪名成立后，被判处监禁30天，折抵为罚款1,500里拉。该判决由R. Rapex法官缓刑五年执行。

意大利大使馆新闻参赞秘书Fennucci，以及体育教练Morelli，各被判处监禁15天，折抵为罚款750里拉。他们的判决未获缓刑，因为他们此前在上海曾有定罪记录。阿尔贝特国王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）海派礼堂（Hai Alai Auditorium）对面“La Moda”裁缝店店主Corigliani，受到同样的判决，缓刑五年。

意大利人承认于5月23日星期五袭击了Leonof先生。Fennucci、Corigliani和Morelli称，他们曾试图强行给这位报人灌下一瓶蓖麻油，“因为这是我们的领袖、法西斯党书记命令我们做的。”Costantini承认下达了命令，并宣称如果“有必要，我会再次这样做，而且命令将再次得到执行。”

Costantini发表了一篇充满激情的演讲，其间手舞足蹈，提高嗓门，并屡次被R. Rapex法官告诫要紧扣相关议题。他猛烈抨击“所谓民主的新闻自由，实则是侮辱的自由”。他说，在上海，“人们使用手头拥有的武器行事”。他冷淡地说，再过几个月，“我们或许会有更多的武器。”

“象征性姿态”

Costantini宣称，法西斯官员对Leonof先生的袭击并非不光彩的行为。他解释说，强行灌蓖麻油是对《字林西报》所刊文章的一种“象征性姿态”回应。他补充说，这次袭击并非出于对Leonof先生的任何个人恩怨。

“我们称上海为国际都市！”他惊呼道。“它是一个国际骗子，因为意大利利益帮助巡逻街道。现实是：在上海，我们有像沙逊（Sassoon）这样的英国犹太人，以及只考虑自身利益的俄国利益集团……”

Costantini引用了《字林西报》中据称反意大利的文章，以及一幅他曾说出现在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）上的漫画，画中描绘日本天皇拉着一辆车。“然而！”他惊呼道，“当日本人向工部局抗议时，工部局却说它无能为力，因为租界内有新闻自由！

他的“轻松玩笑”

“新闻自由！这是侮辱的自由！”他再次陷入修辞性的长篇大论，其中提到了墨索里尼，戏剧性地向法官挥动手臂，再次被后者告诫不要偏离主题，并严厉批评了《字林西报》“非正式记录”（Off the Record）专栏中的“轻松玩笑”。

Leonof先生担任自己的辩护律师。他解释说，撰写社论不在他的职责范围内；因此，他对意大利人提出异议的那篇社论不负责任。他还指出，对报纸刊登内容负责的是管理层，而非其雇员。

Rapex法官宣读了此前媒体报导的事件事实，讲述意大利人如何将Leonof先生诱至大西路意大利俱乐部后方的一块空地，试图强迫他喝下一瓶蓖麻油，并在其拒绝服从命令时对他进行了殴打。

Leonof质问Costantini

Costantini否认有任何造成Leonof先生身体伤害的意图。他解释说，他们只是想让他喝下蓖麻油。“那么，如果我转身走开，”Leonof先生问他，“你们会使用武力吗？”Costantini承认他们会。

他随后表示，他确信Leonof先生撰写了那篇有争议的社论，因为他知道Leonof先生也撰写“非正式记录”专栏的文章。“你承认一个人可能既写‘非正式记录’又写社论的可能性吗？”Leonof先生问他。Costantini给予了肯定的回答。

“那么，”Leonof先生……

JUL 1 1941

Italians Sentenced For
Assault On Mr. Leonof

Fascist Party Secretary, Together With Three Others
Meted Out Suspended Term Or Fines; “China
Press” Insulted Italian Honour

Found guilty of violence on the person of Mr. George Leonof, City Editor of the “China Press,” G. Costantini, Secretary of the Italian Fascist party here, and three of his compatriots, were given suspended sentences in the Italian Consular Court by Judge R. Rapex yesterday morning.

The Fascist party secretary was given a 30-day gaol term or a fine of 1,500 lire suspended for five years, while the other three, P. Corigliani, owner of the La Moda tailor shop on Avenue du Roi Albert, Morelli, a physical culture instructor, and one named Penucci were sentenced to 15 days imprisonment or a fine of 750 lire each, also suspended for five years.

Mr. Leonof, it will be recalled, complained to the Italian Court that on May 23, he was lured by the quartette to a vacant plot of land adjoining the Italian Centre on Great Western Road and efforts made to force him to consume a bottle of castor oil. The four men, failing in the attempt, assaulted Mr. Leonof, whose clothes were subsequently smeared with the liquid.

On the witness stand Corigliani fully displayed his oratorical abilities when he gave the Court his motive for the violence. The “China Press,” he argued, is an American registered paper, and since that country is neutral, no reason could be seen for the wholesale attacks on the honour of Italians.

In various articles and in the “Off the Record” (exhibited in Court) insults to the honour of the Italian King, Signor Mussolini and the Royal Navy are frequently seen and pass in this international city without any criticism from the authorities who must realize how deeply this perpetual insult is felt by the local community.

Castor Oil As Weapon

Corigliani continued to say that his only intentions were to make Mr. Leonof consume the castor oil which, at that, was only used as a means of attracting public attention to the fact that the “China Press” was printing articles inadmissible, deeply defamatory and totally insulting to Italians. Castor oil, accused added, was meant to be a “something to draw the attention of the public and to punish the author of abuses.” The same medicament, accused concluded, was a “mild” weapon.

Corigliani, cross-examined by Mr. Leonof as to why the quartette had actually picked on him as the victim of their wrath, pointed to the “China Press” “Off the Record” column, saying that Mr. Leonof was in charge of it and was also a co-author of items there.

“Freedom Of Insult”

When Mr. Leonof reminded Corigliani that since the “China Press” is an American paper, it has freedom of press and expression, the Fascist official flew into a rage, saying “Freedom of the Press! What is it? It is Freedom of Insult.” He added that if someone enjoyed freedom to insult the glory of Italy, he, Corigliani, had freedom to feed all defaulters with castor oil.

Jews, Jews And Jews

When Judge R. Rapex, having examined all the accused, offered Corigliani to sum up the case for the defence, the latter outdid himself and, going into a wealth of rhetoric, started his speech by blaming the administrative and social structure of Shanghai, an “International City governed by British Jews, American Jews and other Jews.”

1941年7月1日

意大利人因袭击Leonof先生被判刑

法西斯党书记连同其他三人
被判处缓刑或罚款；《字林西报》侮辱意大利荣誉

G. Costantini，此处意大利法西斯党书记，及其三名同胞，因对《字林西报》本市版编辑George Leonof先生实施人身暴力罪名成立，于昨日上午在意国领事法庭被R. Rapex法官判处缓刑。

该法西斯党书记被判处监禁30天或罚款1,500里拉，缓刑五年；其余三人，即阿尔贝特国王路“La Moda”裁缝店店主P. Corigliani、体育教练Morelli，以及一名名为Penucci的人，各被判处监禁15天或罚款750里拉，同样缓刑五年。

回顾可知，Leonof先生向意大利法庭投诉称，5月23日，他被这四人诱至大西路意大利中心附近的一块空地，对方试图强迫他服用一瓶蓖麻油。四人尝试失败后，殴打了Leonof先生，其衣物随后被该液体弄脏。

在证人席上，Corigliani在向法院陈述其暴力动机时充分展示了他的演说才能。他辩称，《字林西报》是一家在美国注册的报纸，既然该国保持中立，就看不出有何理由对意大利人的荣誉进行全盘攻击。

在多篇文章以及“非正式记录”（已在法庭展示）中，经常可以看到对意大利国王、墨索里尼先生和皇家海军的侮辱，而这些在这个国际都市中未经当局任何批评便得以通过，当局必须意识到当地社区对这种持续侮辱的感受有多么深刻。

蓖麻油作为武器

Corigliani继续说，他的唯一意图是让Leonof先生服用蓖麻油，而这只是作为一种手段，以引起公众注意《字林西报》正在刊登对意大利人来说不可接受、极具诽谤性和完全侮辱性的文章这一事实。被告补充说，蓖麻油意在成为“某种引起公众注意并惩罚滥用权力者的东西”。被告总结说，同一种药物是一种“温和”的武器。

在Leonof先生就为何这四人专门挑选他作为愤怒受害者进行交叉质询时，Corigliani指向《字林西报》的“非正式记录”专栏，称Leonof先生负责该专栏，并且也是其中内容的共同作者。

“侮辱的自由”

当Leonof先生提醒Corigliani，既然《字林西报》是美国报纸，它拥有新闻和表达自由时，这位法西斯官员勃然大怒，说道：“新闻自由！那是什么？那是侮辱的自由。”他补充说，如果有人享有侮辱意大利荣耀的自由，那么他，Corigliani，就有自由用蓖麻油喂所有违规者。

犹太人，犹太人，还是犹太人

当R. Rapex法官在审问完所有被告后，让Corigliani为辩方做总结陈词时，后者超越自我，运用大量修辞，开始他的演讲，指责上海的行政和社会结构是一个“由英国犹太人、美国犹太人和其他犹太人治理的国际都市”。

CHINA PRESS.
JUN 10 1941.

Italians Face Court Today
On Leonof Assault Charge

G. Constantini, Secretary of the Italian Fascist Party here, will face the judge of the Italian Consular Court at 10:30 a.m. today together with three other Italians Corigliani, Pasucci and Morelli on a charge of assault brought against them by Mr. George Leonof, city editor of THE CHINA PRESS.

Mr. Leonof was attacked on Friday, May 23, by the four Italians, who said they would "punish" him for writing an allegedly anti-Italian editorial. Although Mr. Leonof pointed out that the writing of editorials in THE CHINA PRESS was outside his province, they tried to force him to drink a bottle of castor oil.

In the struggle that ensued, Mr. Leonof was knocked down and bruised about the head, while his suit was smeared with the castor oil they unsuccessfully tried to pour down his throat, the journalist reported. They then warned him not to report the incident.

Mr. Leonof made a complete report of the case at Bubbling Well police station, and next day lodged charges of assault against the Italians in the Italian Consular Court. It was understood that the four Italians did not deny trying to force Mr. Leonof to drink the castor oil, but claimed before Judge R. Rapex that it was the journalist who started the fight.

1941年6月10日。

意大利人今日因列昂诺夫遇袭案出庭

此处意大利法西斯党书记G.康斯坦蒂尼（G. Constantini）将于今日上午10时30分，与另外三名意大利人科里利亚尼（Corigliani）、帕苏奇（Pasucci）和莫雷利（Morelli）一同在意大利领事法庭法官面前受审，罪名是遭到《字林西报》城市版编辑乔治·列昂诺夫（George Leonof）先生指控的袭击罪。

CHINA PRESS
MAY 30 1931

Leonof's Italian Assailants
To Face Trial On June 10

The date for the trial of the
four Italians who last Friday
evening assaulted Mr. George
Leonof, city editor of THE CHINA
PRESS, after he had refused to
comply with their demand that
he drink a bottle of castor oil
has been set for June 10, Judge
R. Ranez of the Italian Consular
Court revealed yesterday.
The four Italians involved are G.
Costantini, secretary of the local
fascist party, P. Corigliani, owner
of the La Moda tailor shop on
Avenue du Roi Albert, a physical
culture instructor named Morelli
and Penuci.
It was learned yesterday that
the four Italians did not deny
their participation in the inci-
dent. They claimed that they
had had no intention of assault-
ing Mr. Leonof, but merely to
administer to him the bottle of
castor oil. They claimed, in
fact, that the affair came to
blows only after Mr. Leonof's
refusal to drink the castor oil,
and that the newsman had
started the fight.
Mr. Leonof was lured to a vacant
lot on Bubbling Well Road, behind
the Italian center on Great Western
Road, Wednesday evening by the
Italian lawyer, G. Costantini. The
three other Italians were waiting
there. Claiming that Mr. Leonof
had written an editorial which
appeared in THE CHINA PRESS on
May 21; and which dealt with their
flag in a derogatory manner they
insisted that the newsman should
drink a large bottle of castor oil
as a punishment for insulting their
monarch.
Despite Mr. Leonof's assertions
that, as city editor, editorial writing
was not part of his work, the four
men assaulted him when he
repeatedly refused to consume the
castor oil. After Mr. Leonof was
hurled to the ground, Morelli sat
on his chest and attempted to pour
the contents of the bottle down his
throat, but only succeeded in get-
ting the oil over Mr. Leonof's face,
coat suit and shirt.

《字林西报》
1931年5月30日

袭击列昂诺夫的意大利人
将于6月10日受审

意大利领事法庭法官R.拉内兹（R. Ranez）昨日透露，四名意大利人于上周五晚袭击了《字林西报》城市版编辑乔治·列昂诺夫先生，起因是他拒绝服从喝下一瓶蓖麻油的要求，此案的审理日期已定为6月10日。涉案的四名意大利人分别是：当地法西斯党书记G.康斯坦蒂尼（G. Costantini）、阿尔伯特国王大道（Avenue du Roi Albert）上La Moda裁缝店店主P.科里利亚尼（P. Corigliani）、一名名为莫雷利（Morelli）的体育教练以及佩努奇（Penuci）。

昨日获悉，这四名意大利人并未否认参与该事件。他们声称无意袭击列昂诺夫先生，只是想让他喝下那瓶蓖麻油。事实上，他们声称，只有在列昂诺夫先生拒绝喝下蓖麻油后，事态才升级为肢体冲突，且是这名新闻工作者先动的手。

周三晚上，意大利律师G.康斯坦蒂尼将列昂诺夫先生诱至静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的一块空地，该地位于大西路（Great Western Road）意大利中心后方。另外三名意大利人在那里等候。他们声称列昂诺夫先生在5月21日的《字林西报》上发表了一篇社论，以贬损的方式提及他们的国旗，并坚持要求这名新闻工作者喝下一大瓶蓖麻油，作为侮辱他们君主的惩罚。

尽管列昂诺夫先生坚称，作为城市版编辑，撰写社论并非其工作内容，但在他反复拒绝饮用蓖麻油后，这四名男子还是袭击了他。列昂诺夫先生被推倒在地后，莫雷利坐在他胸口，试图将瓶中之物灌入他的喉咙，但只成功地将油泼在了列昂诺夫先生的脸上、外套西装和衬衫上。

Fascist Leader to

An interesting sequel to the recent
experience of Mr. George Leonoff,

法西斯领袖将在本地出庭

据昨日获悉，《字林西报》城市版编辑乔治·列昂诺夫（George Leonoff）先生近期遭遇一事有了有趣的后续。据其向警方报告，在一篇被描述为贬损意大利国王的文章发表后，他被诱骗至市郊并遭到四名意大利人的袭击。此案将于6月16日在意大利领事法庭审理。包括据称为当地法西斯党书记的G.康斯坦蒂尼在内的四名意大利人，将面临袭击罪的指控。

Assault Complaint Lodged By
Leonof With Italian Court

A complaint for criminal as-
sault was yesterday lodged with
Judge R. Rapex of the Italian
Consular Court here by Mr.
George Leonof, City Editor of
THE CHINA PRESS, against the
four Italians who assaulted him
on a vacant lot in the Western
district Friday evening.

The identity of the four Italian
assailants was ascertained yester-
day. The leader of the quartet was
Mr. G. Costantini, a prominent
figure in Fascist circles here. He
telephoned Mr. Leonof on Friday
afternoon, asking for an appoint-
ment at 4 p.m. at the New Royal
Hotel. The appointment was post-
poned by two hours, and when it
was held three uninvited guests
turned up to help Mr. Costantini
attack Mr. Leonof.

The second member of the
group was believed to have been
an Italian called Benuchi. Also
included were a tailor con-
nected with an Italian out-
fitter on Avenue du Roi Albert,
and an Italian physical culture
trainer.

Mr. Leonof was yesterday told by
the Italian authorities that he would
be informed once the wheels of
justice had been set rolling. Mean-
while, he explained, "there has still
been no trouble with my digestive
system."

It will be recalled that Mr. Leonof
was lured from his office Friday
evening by Mr. Costantini, who first
made an appointment with him at
the New Royal Hotel. The two met
at the Palace Hotel because the
original rendezvous was inconveni-
ently located, and met again outside
the New Royal Hotel an hour later.

The Italian invited Mr. Leonof to
stroll over to the Italian Club for
a chat, and the two started off.
They were joined by the Italian
physical instructor, the tailor and
Mr. Benuchi. Upon reaching a
vacant lot of ground, a bottle of cas-
tor oil was pulled out and an at-
tempt was made to force the con-
tents down Mr. Leonof's throat. A
fight ensued between the four Ita-
lians on the one hand and Mr.
Leonof on the other.

The noise emerged from the meet-
ing, and several passers-by inter-
vened. He reported the matter to police
who arrested the men concerned at
the Central Station.

26 - 141

列昂诺夫向意大利法庭提起袭击申诉

《字林西报》城市版编辑乔治·列昂诺夫先生昨日向本地意大利领事法庭的拉佩克斯（R. Rapex）法官提起刑事袭击申诉，控告周五晚上在西区一块空地上袭击他的四名意大利人。

这四名意大利袭击者的身份已于昨日查明。这群人的头目是G.康斯坦蒂尼先生，他是本地法西斯圈子里的一位知名人物。他于周五下午致电列昂诺夫先生，约定下午4点在新皇家酒店（New Royal Hotel）见面。约会时间推迟了两小时，当会面进行时，三名不速之客出现，协助康斯坦蒂尼先生袭击列昂诺夫先生。

据信，该团伙的第二名成员是一名叫贝努奇（Benuchi）的意大利人。此外还包括一名与阿尔伯特国王大道上一家意大利服装店有关的裁缝，以及一名意大利体育教练。

意大利当局昨日告知列昂诺夫先生，一旦司法程序启动，他将得到通知。与此同时，他解释道：“我的消化系统至今仍未出现任何问题。”

回顾此前情况，周五晚上，康斯坦蒂尼先生先将列昂诺夫先生从其办公室诱出，最初约定在新皇家酒店见面。由于原定地点不便，两人在皇宫酒店（Palace Hotel）会面，一小时后又在新皇家酒店外再次见面。

这名意大利人邀请列昂诺夫先生去意大利俱乐部散步聊天，两人随即出发。途中，意大利体育教练、那名裁缝和贝努奇先生加入了他们。到达一块空地后，有人拿出一瓶蓖麻油，并试图将其内容物强行灌入列昂诺夫先生的喉咙。随后，四名意大利人与列昂诺夫先生之间发生了打斗。

打斗声引起了注意，几名路人介入干预。他向警方报告了此事，警方在中央捕房逮捕了相关人员。

Victim of Assault
Files Complaint

It was learned yesterday that Mr.
George Leonoff, City Editor of the
"China Press" had filed a complaint
with Judge R. Rapex, of the Italian

Messrs. G. Constantini, Benuchi, P.

袭击受害者提交诉状

据悉，《字林西报》城市版编辑乔治·列昂诺夫（George Leonoff）先生已向上海意大利领事法庭的拉佩克斯（R. Rapex）法官提交诉状，控告G.康斯坦蒂尼（G. Constantini）、贝努奇（Benuchi）、阿尔伯特国王大道La Moda裁缝店店主P.科里利亚尼（P. Corigliani）以及体育教练莫雷利（Morelli）等先生。指控称，这些人于周五晚上将他诱至静安寺路新皇家酒店对面的一块空地，并试图强迫他喝下一瓶蓖麻油，作为对他所谓反意大利社论的惩罚；他们称该社论于周三刊登在《字林西报》上，并认为列昂诺夫先生对此负责。

当列昂诺夫先生拒绝服从他们的要求时，这四名男子握拳袭击了他，其中一人捡起一块砖头多次击打他，直到其他人命令其停止。随后，袭击者建议列昂诺夫先生不要向警方报案。受害者无视了这一警告，向静安寺巡捕房报告了此案，随后向领事法官提交了诉状。
