SHANGHAI TIMES
MAY 25 1941

Local Scribe Charges Four
Italians With Assault

Sequel To Drama Of Revenge Reveals Dangerous
Potentialities; Anti-Italian Editorial

Sputtering through broken lips, vows of vengeance a Shanghai scribe on Friday night spat out a story of irate reaction to the acid quill reminiscent of the frontier times of Horace Greely.

Yesterday Mr. George Leonof, social satellite and City Editor of the "China Press," swore out charges of assault against four prominent Italian citizens.

Thus was set a dangerous spark to tinder dry antagonisms in Shanghai, a neutral international city, between the two opposing camps of the European holocaust.

Charging brutal assault, Mr. Leonof named four prominent Italians, one a well-known lawyer, another a member of the staff of the Italian Consulate, a third a brawny physical culture instructor.

Leonoff, reputedly still battered from the pummelling he took despite his spirited resistance against courageous odds of four to one, claims he was branded as the author of an editorial appearing in Thursday's issue of the morning contemporary adjudged derogatory to King Victor Emanuel of Italy. Leonof denies the accusation.

Gone With The Wind?

Meanwhile a prominent radio broadcaster last night declared that the Italian Consul-General had declined responsibility for the acts of Italian citizens, the latter allegedly implying that Italians had been goaded beyond control. The broadcaster said that he himself had been mentioned as beyond toleration.

Though, in spite of the ugly omen of things, level-headed citizens believed that the storm would blow over and that the European War could be kept from extending to Shanghai in the shape of miniature imbroglios, it was not forgotten that the Latin blood had been fired in two previous incidents within the present year. Heads were roundly cracked in a brawl between Italian and American defence units at Yulside in a local dance hall, while only last month the seizure by the Italians of the Yugoslavian freighter "Dalmatia" created a situation pregnant with danger.

Mr. Leonof, resting in his apartment in Hamilton House yesterday, explained that he had not retained counsel, since this was a criminal proceeding and would be undertaken by the Italian Consular prosecutor. Mr. Leonof, who is understood to be a Soviet citizen, was reputedly given quite a pummelling, but suffered no serious injuries.

Lured To His Doom

Mr. Leonof, a well-known Shanghai scribe of still youthful years, is known to have had some previous difficulties with the Italians officially in connection with publicity work. He denies, however, that he has any serious acquaintance with any of his alleged attackers. The latter, it is said, could be learnt, were not of the same class.

ance alluded to, he says. Mr. Leonof explained that his duties do not involve the writing of editorials.

At about 3.30 p.m. on Friday, Mr. Leonof says, he received a telephone call at the office, requesting him to meet at the Royal Hotel, 2,004 Bubbling Well Road, a Mr. Constantini, local Italian barrister, and one of the accused. The caller said that he wished to "ask him something about an Italian paper."

Mr. Leonof could not go at the time, but made an appointment for 6.30 at the same place. When he arrived, he met Constantini, who invited him over to the Italian Club to have a talk. When however, they reached a vacant lot near the Italian Centre, they were met by three other Italians, whereupon his escort allegedly said:

"I'm frightfully sorry to have tricked you, but we wanted to talk to you."

The four men then accused him of writing anti-Italian articles, and took particular umbrage at the editorial referred to above.

Puts Up Struggle

Though Mr. Leonof stoutly denied that he was responsible for the editorial, the quartette, with sardonic politeness, said that they were sorry, but they were obliged to chastise him. When he retorted against their numerical superiority, they assured him that "they did not want to injure him, but they were obliged to make him drink this." Whereupon they produced a bottle with a gummy, viscous oil, the bane of every urchin, and the famed Mussolini antidote to outspokenness.

The victim determinedly resisted, but they suavely assured him that he must drain the sticky contents to the dregs. They then laid hands on him, and attempted to force it down his gullet. One of the quartette, Leonof alleges, seized a brick, but was restrained by his colleagues.

In the scuffle the valiant scribe won a moral victory, for though the sticky syrup was smattered over his hair, face and clothes, none of it found its mark. Nevertheless, the militant scribe suffered sundry bruises and scratches, for treatment of which he proceeded to the Country Hospital.

Was Warned

When he was finally freed, he recalls that his attackers were told them he would report the matter to the police. They warned him against such rashness, and carried out his threat.

《上海泰晤士报》
1941年5月25日

本地文人指控四名意大利人殴打

复仇剧的续集揭示了危险的潜在可能；反意大利社论

透过破裂的嘴唇嘶嘶作响，一名上海文人在周五晚上吐露了一个故事，讲述了对尖酸笔触的愤怒反应，让人想起霍勒斯·格里利（Horace Greely）时代的边疆岁月。

昨日，《大美晚报》（China Press）社交界活跃人士兼本市新闻编辑乔治·莱昂诺夫（George Leonof）先生宣誓控告四名知名意大利公民殴打。

由此，在上海这座中立的国际城市，在欧洲浩劫的两个对立阵营之间，干燥的敌对情绪被点燃了一颗危险的火花。

莱昂诺夫先生指控遭受残酷殴打，点名四名知名意大利人，其中一位是著名律师，另一位是意大利领事馆职员，第三位是一名魁梧的体育教练。

据称，莱昂诺夫尽管在以一对四的悬殊劣势下英勇抵抗，但仍遭痛殴，目前仍有余痛。他声称自己被指认为周四早间某报刊载的一篇社论的作者，该社论被认为有损意大利国王维托里奥·埃马努埃莱（Victor Emanuel）的尊严。莱昂诺夫否认这一指控。

随风而逝？

与此同时，一位知名广播员昨晚宣称，意大利总领事已拒绝为意大利公民的行为承担责任，后者据称暗示意大利人已被激怒至失控地步。该广播员称，他自己也被提及为不可容忍之人。

尽管事态有不祥之兆，头脑冷静的市民相信风暴终将过去，欧洲战争可以通过避免小型纠纷的形式而不蔓延至上海。但人们没有忘记，在今年之前的两起事件中，拉丁血统的热情已被点燃。在一家本地舞厅，意大利和美国防卫人员在“Yulside”（音译）发生斗殴，多人头部受重创；而上个月，意大利人扣押南斯拉夫货轮“达尔马提亚号”（Dalmatia），造成了充满危险的局面。

莱昂诺夫先生昨日在其汉密尔顿公寓（Hamilton House）休息时解释说，他未聘请律师，因为这是刑事诉讼，将由意大利领事检察官负责。据悉莱昂诺夫为苏联公民，据称遭到相当程度的痛殴，但未受重伤。

诱入绝境

莱昂诺夫先生是一位尚处青年的上海知名文人，众所周知，他此前在宣传工作方面与意大利官方发生过一些摩擦。然而，他否认与任何所谓的袭击者有深交。据说，后者的阶层与他所暗示的并不相同。

他说。莱昂诺夫解释说，他的职责不涉及撰写社论。

莱昂诺夫先生说，周五下午约3点30分，他在办公室接到一个电话，要求他在静安寺路2004号的新皇家酒店（Royal Hotel）会见当地意大利律师、被告之一的康斯坦蒂尼（Constantini）先生。来电者称希望“向他询问有关一份意大利报纸的事”。

莱昂诺夫当时无法前往，但约定于6点30分在同一地点见面。当他到达时，会见了康斯坦蒂尼，后者邀请他去意大利俱乐部谈谈。然而，当他们到达意大利中心附近的一块空地时，遇到了另外三名意大利人，此时他的陪同者据称说道：

“非常抱歉骗了你，但我们想和你谈谈。”

随后，这四名男子指责他撰写反意大利文章，并对上述提到的社论特别感到愤慨。

奋力反抗

尽管莱昂诺夫先生坚决否认对该社论负责，但这四人带着讽刺的礼貌表示很遗憾，但他们不得不惩罚他。当他反驳他们以多欺少时，他们向他保证“他们不想伤害他，但他们必须让他喝下这个”。于是，他们拿出一瓶装有粘稠胶状油的瓶子，这是每个顽童的祸害，也是墨索里尼对付直言不讳者的著名“解毒剂”。

受害者坚决抵抗，但他们温和地坚持说他必须将粘腻的内容物喝得一滴不剩。随后他们动手抓住他，试图强行灌入他的喉咙。莱昂诺夫指控，四人中的一人抓起一块砖头，但被同伴制止。

在混战中，这位勇敢的文人赢得了道德上的胜利，因为虽然粘腻的糖浆溅到了他的头发、脸部和衣服上，但并没有真正灌进去。尽管如此，这位好斗的文人身上多处淤青和抓伤，为此他前往乡村医院（Country Hospital）接受治疗。

曾受警告

当他最终获释时，他记得袭击者得知他将向警方报告此事。他们警告他不要如此鲁莽，但他还是执行了他的威胁。

有问题的社论引用了芝加哥《每日新闻》记者“惠特克”（Whittaker）的“报道”，该记者最近被罗马驱逐出境，他抨击了纳粹对……的统治……

四名被告——一名律师、一名外交官和……

25 8 71

Leonof Beaten
Up By Italians
In West Area

Mr. George Leonof, City Editor of THE CHINA PRESS was injured yesterday at 6:30 p.m. when four Italians attacked him after charging that he was responsible for an editorial appearing in Wednesday's CHINA PRESS which revealed the extent of German influence and control in Italy.

Late last night it was learned that Mr. Leonof had sustained various cuts and bruises on his face and head and had been drenched in castor oil.

Mr. Leonof stated that at 3:30 p.m. yesterday an Italian named Costantini telephoned him at the office and asked him to meet him at the New Royal Hotel at 2004 Bubbling Well Road, as he wished to ask him something about an Italian paper.

Lured To Hotel

Mr. Leonof replied that he could not comply as he was busy, but agreed to meet Costantini at the Palace Hotel at 5 p.m. At 5:20 the Italian rushed in and said that he was sorry but he had another previous engagement and asked Mr. Leonof to meet him at the New Royal Hotel at 6:30.

When Mr. Leonof arrived at the hotel at 6:30 Costantini was waiting in front of the building. The Italian invited him to go over to the Italian Club to have their talk. They reached a vacant lot adjoining the Italian Center and were met by three other Italians.

At this point Costantini said, "I'm frightfully sorry to have tricked you, but we wanted to talk to you," Mr. Leonof reported. The men then charged him with writing the allegedly anti-Italian articles in THE CHINA PRESS, and pointed out in particular the editorial concerning the growth of German influence in Italy.

Although Mr. Leonof steadily denied that he had anything to do with the editorials in the paper and maintained that as City Editor his job was concerned entirely with city news, the men stated that they would be forced to punish him.

Use Castor Oil

"I then said that I supposed they could, owing to their numerical superiority," Mr. Leonof stated. However, the men said that they did not want to beat him but merely desired him to drink "this" and pulled out a large bottle of castor oil.

"I said that I wouldn't drink it. I didn't like it, and that even if I did there was too much of it," Mr. Leonof reported. "They then tried to force it down me, but I resisted and the fight ensued," Mr. Leonof said. During the scrap, according to Mr. Leonof, one of the men picked up a brick and started to hit me with it, but the others yelled at him and he dropped it."

Following the incident, "I told them they were fools and I reported to the Bubbling Well Police Station," he continued. From there Mr. Leonof went to the Country Hospital where he received medical attention and then returned to the police station and proceeded on home.

Warned By Italians

Prior to leaving the scene, the Italians warned their victim not to report the affair to the police.

In addition to Costantini Mr. Leonof identified one of the men as the proprietor of an Italian tailor shop and said that he recognized another one of them, but had never seen the fourth one before.

The editorial in question quoted the report of Mr. John T. Whitaker, correspondent of the Chicago Daily News who was expelled from Rome where he worked for some time. The editorial commented on the fact that Nazis had gained almost complete control of the Italian Foreign Office, the Ministries of War, Communications and Finance. It also revealed that Italians in Africa were ready for a separate peace but this was forestalled by quick action on the part of Chancellor Hitler.

25 8 71

莱昂诺夫在西区
被意大利人殴打

《大美晚报》本市新闻编辑乔治·莱昂诺夫先生昨日下午6点30分受伤，当时四名意大利人袭击了他，指控他对周三《大美晚报》上发表的一篇社论负责，该社论揭露了德国在意大利的影响和控制程度。

昨晚获悉，莱昂诺夫先生面部和头部有多处割伤和淤青，并被浇满了蓖麻油。

莱昂诺夫先生表示，昨天下午3点30分，一名叫康斯坦蒂尼（Costantini）的意大利人打电话到办公室找他，要求他在静安寺路2004号的新皇家酒店见面，因为他想向他询问有关一份意大利报纸的事。

诱至酒店

莱昂诺夫先生回答说，他因忙碌无法前往，但同意下午5点在宫殿酒店（Palace Hotel）与康斯坦蒂尼见面。5点20分，这名意大利人冲进来，说很抱歉，他另有 prior engagement（原文如此，意为已有约会），并请莱昂诺夫先生于6点30分在新皇家酒店见面。

当莱昂诺夫先生于6点30分到达酒店时，康斯坦蒂尼正在大楼前等候。这名意大利人邀请他去意大利俱乐部谈话。他们到达毗邻意大利中心的一块空地时，遇到了另外三名意大利人。

莱昂诺夫先生报告说，此时康斯坦蒂尼说：“非常抱歉骗了你，但我们想和你谈谈。”随后，这些人指控他在《大美晚报》上撰写所谓的反意大利文章，并特别指出了关于德国在意大利影响力增长的社论。

尽管莱昂诺夫先生一直否认自己与报社的社论有任何关系，并坚称作为本市新闻编辑，他的工作完全涉及本市新闻，但这些人表示他们将不得不惩罚他。

使用蓖麻油

“我当时说，我想他们可以，因为他们人多势众，”莱昂诺夫先生说。然而，这些人说他们不想打他，只是希望他喝下“这个”，并拿出了一大瓶蓖麻油。

“我说我不喝。我不喜欢它，而且即使我想喝，量也太多了，”莱昂诺夫先生报告说。“然后他们试图强行灌我，但我进行了抵抗，随即发生了打斗，”莱昂诺夫先生说。据莱昂诺夫先生说，在争斗过程中，其中一人捡起一块砖头开始砸他，但其他人大声喝止，他便扔下了砖头。”

事件发生后，“我告诉他们他们是傻瓜，并向静安寺巡捕房报了案，”他继续说道。随后，莱昂诺夫先生前往乡村医院接受医疗救治，然后返回巡捕房，之后回家。

受意大利人警告

在离开现场之前，意大利人警告受害者不要向警方报告此事。

除了康斯坦蒂尼外，莱昂诺夫还指认其中一人为一家意大利裁缝店的店主，并称他认出了另一人，但以前从未见过第四人。

有问题的社论引用了约翰·T·惠特克（John T. Whitaker）先生的报道，他是芝加哥《每日新闻》的记者，曾在罗马工作一段时间后被驱逐出境。该社论评论了纳粹几乎完全控制意大利外交部、陆军部、交通部和财政部的事实。它还透露，在非洲的意大利人准备单独媾和，但希特勒总理的快速行动阻止了这一情况。

Vicious Attack on Local
Newspaperman by Fascists

RESENTMENT among Italian Fascist circles here over recent press editorials which they characterized as derogatory to the King of Italy flared into open violence yesterday afternoon when four Italians, including a Fascist leader, lured Mr. George Leonoff, City Editor of the "China Press" to a vacant plot of land near the Italian Centre where they assaulted him after accusing him of writing the articles. That the assailants were bent on taking the law into their own hands was evidenced by the fact that they refused to accept the explanation of their victim that he was not responsible for the appearance of the articles and did not write them.

At 3.30 p.m. Mr. Leonoff received a call from the secretary of the Fascist party, who wanted to talk to him about the "Daily News", an Italian paper. The receiver of the message enquired where they could meet. The caller suggested the New Royal Hotel. The rendezvous being an inconvenient place for Mr. Leonoff as it was rather far from town. Mr. Leonoff suggested that they should meet somewhere downtown. They finally agreed to meet at 5 p.m. at the Palace Hotel Bar.

At the time and place appointed Mr. Leonoff met the caller, who remarked that he was terribly sorry, but that he had made a previous engagement and could not discuss things with the newsman then. It was suggested that they should meet again at 6-30 p.m. at the New Royal to which Mr. Leonoff agreed to go. When he kept the appointment he accompanied the Italian, at the latter's request to a vacant plot of land across the street within sight of the Italian Centre where he agreed to go with his companion.

A Bottle of Castor Oil

After they had proceeded a little distance three other Italians appeared on the scene. The first Italian according to Mr. Leonoff, then expressed regret at having to treat him in that way, and suggested that he would have to be punished for insulting the King of Italy in a newspaper editorial. The scribe replied that he did not know what the Italian was talking about when the Italian told him about a recent editorial in the press. Mr. Leonoff explained that as city editor, he was in no way concerned with the writing of editorials. "Someone told me you did it" was the prompt rejoinder. According to Mr. Leonoff the Italian repeated that he should be punished for his indiscretion and he replied that this should be an easy matter since he was outnumbered by four to one.

In a statement which Mr. Leonoff subsequently made to the Police, another member of the quartette then took out from his pocket a bottle of castor oil and suggested that he should gulp it all down which he refused following which the Italian attempted to exert force to make him swallow the contents of the bottle with the result that it was spilled over his clothes and hair. Mr. Leonoff went on to state that the Italians without further explanation proceeded to pummel him, one of them even picking up a brick to knock him on the head, but was restrained by one of his companions.

Mr. Leonoff told the "North China Daily News" last night that his assailants attacked him with clenched fists and said that when it was all over that he remarked to them that they were very brave. Leaving the scene of the assault he went to the Bubbling Well Police station where he made a report of the entire incident.

法西斯分子对本地报人实施恶性袭击

此处意大利法西斯圈子因近期报刊社论被其指称为侮辱意大利国王而心生怨恨，这种情绪于昨日下午演变为公开暴力。四名意大利人（其中包括一名法西斯头目）将《字林西报》（China Press）本市新闻编辑乔治·莱昂诺夫（George Leonoff）先生诱骗至意国中心（Italian Centre）附近的一块空地，在指控他撰写了这些文章后对他进行了殴打。袭击者意图私自执法，这一点从他们拒绝接受受害者的解释——即他对文章的刊登不负责任且并未撰写这些文章——这一事实中可见一斑。

下午3时30分，莱昂诺夫先生接到法西斯党秘书的电话，对方希望与他谈谈意大利报纸《每日新闻》（Daily News）。接电话的人询问见面地点。打电话的人建议在新皇家酒店（New Royal Hotel）见面。由于该地点离市区较远，对莱昂诺夫先生来说不太方便，他便建议在市中心的某个地方见面。双方最终约定下午5时在汇中饭店（Palace Hotel）酒吧见面。

在约定的时间和地点，莱昂诺夫先生见到了打电话的人，后者表示非常抱歉，但因已有 prior 约定，当时无法与这位新闻工作者商谈。有人建议他们下午6时30分再在新皇家酒店见面，莱昂诺夫先生同意前往。当他赴约时，应那名意大利人的请求，他陪同后者穿过街道，来到意国中心视线范围内的一块空地，他同意与同伴前往该处。

一瓶蓖麻油

他们走了一小段距离后，另外三名意大利人出现在现场。据莱昂诺夫先生称，第一名意大利人随后表示不得不这样对待他深感遗憾，并指出他必须因在报纸社论中侮辱意大利国王而受到惩罚。这位撰稿人回答说，当那名意大利人向他提及最近报刊上的一篇社论时，他不知道对方在说什么。莱昂诺夫先生解释说，作为本市新闻编辑，他与社论的撰写毫无关系。“有人告诉我就是你干的，”对方立即反驳道。据莱昂诺夫先生称，那名意大利人重申他应因自己的轻率行为受到惩罚，他回答说既然对方以四敌一，这应该是件容易的事。

在莱昂诺夫随后向警方所作的陈述中，那四人中的另一名成员从口袋里掏出一瓶蓖麻油，建议他将其全部吞下，他拒绝了，随后那名意大利人试图强行让他吞下瓶中之物，结果液体洒在了他的衣服和头发上。莱昂诺夫先生继续陈述称，那些意大利人没有进一步解释便动手殴打他，其中一人甚至捡起一块砖头要砸他的头，但被其一名同伴制止。

莱昂诺夫先生昨晚告诉《字林西报》（North China Daily News），袭击者握紧拳头攻击他，并称当一切结束时，他对他们说他们非常勇敢。离开袭击现场后，他前往静安寺捕房（Bubbling Well Police station），就整个事件作了报告。

REPORT

S.1, Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date May 13, 1941.

SUBJECT: China Press - Publication of a paragraph on projected publication of book on S.M.C. Gaol

In connection with a paragraph appearing in the China Press "Off The Record" column of 9 May 1941, enquiries have learned that the person contemplating writing the volume is Charles Vivien Hutchinson, unrecognised American.

Hutchinson has long been known to the Police as a trouble maker and was released from Ward Road Gaol in June 1940 after receiving a sentence of two years in the 1st Special District Court for receiving stolen property. In connection with this case, he has initiated legal proceedings in the Court of Consuls, claiming damages of $75,000.00 for wrongful arrest and imprisonment. He is well known to the writer of this report as a braggart with a "persecution complex," and although the publication of such a volume is a venture likely to commend itself to him, I strongly doubt that he has the ability or the tenacity of purpose to carry it through.

（批：Sent 14/5.）
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH 1941）
（批：10. 14/5.）

R. G. Hanning

特别捕房第1分站。档案号.................... 日期 1941年5月13日。

主题：《字林西报》——刊登关于计划出版有关工部局监狱一书的一段文字

针对1941年5月9日《字林西报》“非正式记录”（Off The Record）专栏中出现的一段文字，经查询获悉，打算撰写该书的人是查尔斯·维维安·哈钦森（Charles Vivien Hutchinson），一名未获承认的美国人。

警方早已知晓哈钦森是一名惹是生非者，他曾在第一特区法院因收受赃物罪被判刑两年，并于1940年6月从提篮桥监狱（Ward Road Gaol）获释。与此案相关，他已在领事法庭提起法律诉讼，声称因非法逮捕和监禁要求赔偿75,000.00美元。本报告撰写者深知他是一个患有“迫害妄想症”的爱吹牛者，虽然出版此类书籍是一项可能令他自我欣赏的冒险举动，但我强烈怀疑他是否有能力或毅力将此书完成。

Thieves' Haven
Nanking Road these days is none-too-safe for shopkeepers and clients alike. The daring robbery in broad daylight on Sunday of a jewelry store near the corner of Fokien Road indicates that this shopping center has come to be some sort of a haven for the ignoble professionals.

Near the bus stop not far from Kwangse Road yesterday, a customer had emerged from a Cantonese food shop with a big package under his arm. Apparently it contained dry or smoked meats. A huge crowd had gathered around the bus stop waiting for the bus. When the bus arrived, the man with the package was standing right along the curb and when the bus door opened, he was the first to enter the vehicle.

At this juncture, some one from behind reached his hand up, tapped the man on the shoulder. By reflex action the man turned his head in response to the tapping. Meanwhile, another man standing to the left, near the bus door, grabbed the package from under the latter's arms circled around the crowd and disappeared.

Bus conductors said they frequently saw this type of robbery perpetrated at the same bus stop.

Expose-To-Be
A local resident who recently left Ward Road Jail after spending more than a year in the Hongkew hoosegow tells OF THE RECORD that he is going to "expose crooked S.M.C. machinations within the confines of the world's biggest penitentiary" in a book that he is preparing to write in the near future. He got the idea, he modestly explains, in his cell a few months after he was imprisoned. He hasn't yet decided on a title for the book, but he expects it to be something dramatic like "Fourteen Months In Ward Jail" or "I Knew Ward Road."

Incidentally, the budding author is already making plans to turn the best-seller-to-be into a movie, though he hasn't yet decided to which of Hollywood's major studios he will sell the story.

窃贼的避风港

如今，南京路对店主和顾客而言都绝非安全之地。周日白天发生在福建路拐角附近一家珠宝店的大胆抢劫案表明，这个购物中心已某种程度地成为了卑鄙职业罪犯的避风港。

昨天，在离广西路不远的公交车站附近，一名顾客腋下夹着一个大包裹从一家广东食品店出来。显然，里面装着干肉或熏肉。一大群人聚集在公交车站等车。当公交车到达时，夹着包裹的男子正站在路边，车门一开，他是第一个上车的人。

就在此时，身后有人伸出手，拍了拍那名男子的肩膀。出于反射动作，男子转头回应拍打。与此同时，另一名站在左侧、靠近车门的人从该男子腋下抢走包裹，绕过人群消失不见。

公交车售票员表示，他们经常看到同一公交车站发生此类抢劫。

即将曝光

一位当地居民在虹口看守所（hoosegow）度过一年多后，最近离开了提篮桥监狱，他向“非正式记录”栏目透露，他正准备在不久的将来写一本书，“揭露这座世界最大监狱范围内的工部局腐败阴谋”。他谦虚地解释说，这个想法是他入狱几个月后在牢房里产生的。他尚未决定书名，但预计会是一个具有戏剧性的名字，如《提篮桥监狱十四个月》或《我了解提篮桥》。

顺便提一下，这位初出茅庐的作家已经在计划将这部未来的畅销书拍成电影，尽管他尚未决定将故事卖给好莱坞哪家主要制片厂。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. J. REGISTRY
No. 8147 2/5

We The People

THE CHINA PRESS welcomes the views of its readers on subjects of the day, but publication in the correspondence column does not mean necessarily that the views expressed by correspondents are those of THE CHINA PRESS:

British Labor Party & India

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS
Sir:—The interest taken in Indian affairs by the “China Press” has not passed unnoticed by your readers although unfortunately this subject is apt to be neglected these days.

Much light is shed on the present policy of the British Labor Party by the ensuing correspondence between Dr. Krishna Menon, Secretary of the India League, prospective Parliamentary candidate for Dundee, and officials of the B.L.P. who withdrew the latter’s candidature.

Of particular interest is the fact that no denial was made by the B.L.P. of the conclusions which the Indian candidate drew as to the underlying reasons for his repudiation.

Mr. G. R. Shepherd, National Agent of the Labor Party, to Mr. Menon:

The National Executive Committee has now considered the report of a Delegation appointed by it to enquire into the reasons which led the Dundee Trades Council and Labor Party to cancel your candidature for one of the Dundee seats.

The National Executive Committee has expressed the view that the procedure followed by the Dundee Trades and Labor Party was wrong and I have been instructed to warn it that before a verdict had been given the party ought to have invited you to have appeared before it to discuss any complaints.

At the same time, the National Executive Committee came to the conclusion that no useful purpose would be served in maintaining your candidature for Dundee, because the necessary confidence and friendliness for a successful candidature does not now exist, and does not seem likely to be brought about.

The National Executive Committee also gave consideration to your political position. It recognises you as a representative of an important section of Indian public opinion and it believes that your first loyalty lies in that direction. Whilst it cannot, even if it had the desire to, question your right as a British subject to seek entrance into the House of Commons, it does not believe that you ought to seek such entry through the British Labor Party. As you know, our Constitution exacts a degree of loyalty and discipline rendered necessary by circumstances. It feels sure, however, you would not claim that, owing to your national allegiance to India, you can give full support to Labor Party policy.

The decision of the National Executive Committee in respect of Dundee endorses and justifies the position created by the action of the Executive Committee of the Dundee Trades Council and Labor Party which the National Executive Committee has been obliged to find wrong. It appears, therefore, that the inquiry which was dragged over a period of eight months was purposeless and unreal as the National Executive Committee has based its decision in respect of Dundee not on the merits of the dispute but on the ground that no useful purpose can be served by maintaining the candidature as a result of the situation created by the admittedly wrong action of the Dundee Executive Committee.

I am therefore unable to understand the significance of your observation that you have been instructed to warn the Dundee Trades and Labor Party as obviously there is no conduct from which it is being restrained or the results of which it need regret.

I consider it necessary to place on record my repudiation of your suggestion that there is any lack of confidence or friendliness between the Dundee Labor Party and Trades Council and myself. On the contrary the facts are quite the reverse and it is the knowledge that I enjoy both the confidence and the friendliness of the General Council as a whole that made it necessary for the Dundee Executive Committee to take its decision without reference to the properly constituted organs of the Party, without adequate notice and by a sparse vote on the Executive itself. I maintain that I enjoy the confidence of the Dundee Trades Council and Labor Party and of the Dundee Labor movement as a whole. I do not, however, any longer seek the recognition by the National Executive of that confidence.

Nor is it correct to say that the action was taken quite independently even by the Dundee Executive Committee. It came not at the inquiry that your officials had instigated and inspired the action and did not even consider that the ordinary courtesy of informing me was part of their duties. The latter part of your letter referring to what you call my “political position” also bears out the fact that the Dundee Executive was being used.

The latter part of your letter raises larger issues which make the situation in regard to Dundee and myself secondary. I consider it more appropriate that I should address my reply on this part of the decision of the National Executive Committee to the Secretary of the Party as it is not in my view merely a question of Party organisation.

I am sending a copy of this letter to Mr. Middleton for his information and in view of the issues involved shall release the correspondence to the press.

KRISHNA MENON
December 16, 1940.

Mr. Menon to Mr. Middleton, Secretary of the Labor Party:

I note that the National Executive Committee has considered my “political position” and come to the conclusion that my “first loyalty lies in India.” In my submission this is not a question of Party organisation.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. J. 登记处
编号 8147 2/5

《我们人民》

《字林西报》欢迎读者就当前时事发表意见，但来信栏刊登的信件并不必然代表《字林西报》所持观点：

英国工党与印度

致《字林西报》编辑
先生：——贵报对印度事务的关注并未逃过读者的眼睛，尽管不幸的是，这一主题近来往往被忽视。

印度联盟秘书、邓迪选区潜在议会候选人克里希纳·梅农博士（Dr. Krishna Menon）与撤销其候选人资格的英国工党官员之间的下述通信，为阐明英国工党当前的政策提供了许多线索。

特别令人感兴趣的事实是，英国工党并未否认这位印度候选人就其被拒绝提名背后的根本原因所作出的结论。

工党全国代理人 G. R. 谢泼德先生致梅农先生：

全国执行委员会现已审议了其指派的一个代表团提交的报告，该代表团负责调查导致邓迪工会理事会和工党取消您作为邓迪席位之一候选人的原因。

全国执行委员会表示，邓迪工会和工党所遵循的程序是错误的，并指示我警告他们，在作出裁决之前，本应邀请您出席并与他们讨论任何投诉。

同时，全国执行委员会得出结论认为，维持您在邓迪的候选人资格不会起到任何有益的作用，因为成功竞选所需的信任和友好关系目前并不存在，且似乎不太可能建立起来。

全国执行委员会还考虑了您的政治立场。它承认您是印度舆论重要部分的代表，并相信您的首要忠诚在于此方向。虽然即使有意愿，它也不能质疑您作为英国臣民寻求进入下议院的权利，但它认为您不应通过英国工党寻求这种进入。如您所知，我们的党章要求一定程度的忠诚和纪律，这是形势所必需的。然而，它确信，由于您对印度的民族效忠，您不会声称能够全力支持工党的政策。

全国执行委员会关于邓迪的决定认可并证明了由邓迪工会理事会和工党执行委员会的行动所造成的局面是正当的，尽管全国执行委员会不得不认定该行动是错误的。因此，看来这项拖延长达八个月的调查是毫无目的且不切实际的，因为全国执行委员会关于邓迪的决定并非基于争议的是非曲直，而是基于这样一个理由：鉴于邓迪执行委员会公认的错误行动所造成的局面，维持候选人资格已无益可言。

因此，我无法理解您所言受到警告的意义，因为显然并没有任何行为需要加以约束，也没有任何后果需要感到遗憾。

我认为有必要记录在案，我驳斥您关于邓迪工党和工会理事会与我之间缺乏信任或友好的说法。相反，事实恰恰相反，正是因为我享有整个总理事会的信任和友好，使得邓迪执行委员会有必要在不参考党内适当组成的机构、未给予充分通知以及执行委员会本身投票人数稀少的情况下作出决定。我坚持认为，我享有邓迪工会理事会和工党以及整个邓迪劳工运动的信任。然而，我不再寻求全国执行委员会对这种信任的认可。

此外，说这一行动完全是由邓迪执行委员会独立采取的也不正确。并非在调查中得知，而是您的官员煽动并激发了这一行动，甚至不认为通知我这一普通礼节是他们职责的一部分。您信中提到所谓我的“政治立场”的后半部分也证实了邓迪执行委员会是被利用的这一事实。

您信件的后半部分提出了更大的问题，使得关于邓迪和我本人的情况变得次要。我认为，更恰当的做法是我将针对全国执行委员会决定中这部分的回复写给党的书记，因为在我看来，这不仅仅是一个党组织的问题。

我将此信的副本发送给米德尔顿先生供其知晓，鉴于所涉及的问题，我将向新闻界公布这些通信往来。

克里希纳·梅农
1940年12月16日。

梅农先生致工党书记米德尔顿先生：

我注意到，全国执行委员会已考虑了我的“政治立场”，并得出结论认为我的“首要忠诚在于印度”。依我之见，这不是一个党组织的问题。

These gross lapses have been con-
demned by the National Executive
Committee, which has been either
unwilling or unable to replace or
discipline those responsible. Mr.
Ramsay MacDonald proclaimed that
India was a "non-party" issue and
made Tory imperialists sanction the
denominator in Indian policy.

Those who came after him have
carried the tradition further and
earned the appreciation of the im-
perialists opposite them. Of this
the pages of Hansard bear ample
testimony.

The National Executive Commit-
tee, however, has hitherto refrained
from openly committing itself to the
position that there is an inherent
contradiction between "Labor Party
Policy" and an allegiance to Social-
ist principles in their application
to India.

The present decision marks a de-
finite change. I am driven to the
inevitable conclusion that it arises
not from my political position—
which is the constant factor—but
from the change in the position
which the National Executive Com-
mittee has now found it necessary
to proclaim.

The closer its links with the im-
perialists the farther it must seek
to drive those who are opponents of
imperialists, of exploitation of man
by man and nation by nation.

This is the moral of your decision.
It is thrown into significant relief
by the fact that the National Exe-
cutive Committee has chosen the
present moment for it. Neither the
Committee nor any of its members
have found it necessary to raise their
voice of protest against the savage
sentence imposed on the foremost
Socialist in India, Pandit Jawaharlal
Nehru.

The implications of the decision
of the National Executive Committee
are far-reaching and concern not
only India or myself—its immediate
subject. They challenge the faith
of Socialists. They strike at the
root of International Socialism.

The National Executive Commit-
tee have now introduced a national
and racial bar into the Labor move-
ment.

Politically, the National Executive
Committee has now declared, beyond
all doubt, that it has its own con-
ception of what it calls the "wel-
fare of the Indian people," and this
conception is incompatible with that
of those who, in its view, owe "na-
tional allegiance" to India. In other
words, Labor Party policy is now de-
clared by its Supreme Executive to
be opposed to the basic conceptions
of self-determination and national
independence of subject peoples,
and at best to be some form of bene-
volent and patronising imperialism.

The ending of imperialism, with
its attendant poverty, exploitation,
race-hatred, wars, its fatal de-
moralisation and hatreds and its poison-
ing of minds, is equally the concern
of the peoples of this country as
it is of those in Malaya, India or
Africa.

The "natural allegiance" of peo-
ples does not divide them; on the
contrary, they are bound of unity in
what is a common struggle which
should be recognized and welcomed
as such by Socialists. The common
foe which exploits them all, with
diverse technique, seeks to divide
them. This is also part of the
technique.

It is pitiable, therefore, that the
National Executive Committee of
the British Labor Party, the prin-
cipal constituent body of the Social-
ist International, should have mis-
directed itself, adopted the categor-
ies of imperialism, and cast itself
in the role of its ally.

I take heart and courage in the
knowledge and belief that this
strange doctrine propounded by the
National Executive Committee will
not find universal acceptance within
the movement

It has been my good fortune to
share the comradeship and to re-
ceive the friendship and confidence
of large numbers of men and
women in the Labor movement who,
I feel sure, will not understand or
accept your doctrine. For, they fully
believe, even if they are not always
given the opportunity to under-
stand, that the "allegiance" to
which you refer arises from our
common aspiration and is part of
our common struggle against a com-
mon foe.

I understand now, even more than
I have hitherto done, that wide and
widening gulf between the National
Executive Committee and those
whom it represents. To these latter,
such services as I am able to render
I shall give without reserve. In
their hearts they do not recognize
your frontiers.

In relation to India my position
remains unchanged. I am unrepent-
ant in my allegiance. I shall con-
tinue to work to bring about the
realization that the struggles of
peoples of all lands is a common
one against common foes, that their
exploiters seek to divide and weaken
them, and that in their unity lies
their strength.

Happily, in India, there is a wide-
spread realisation of this view. The
people of India have no quarrel with
the people of this country. Their
struggle is directed against an ex-
ploiting and oppressive system.
Even in the days of the brutal re-
pression under the second Labor
Government the national movement
in India drew a sharp distinction
between those who were then res-
ponsible for British policy in India
and those whom they claimed to re-
present.

I am not without hope that time,
events and, most important of all
the people will forge that unity—
which their foes dread—and con-
quer.

In that hope I live and strive.
Yours sincerely, (signed),
V. K. Krishna Menon
December 28, 1930.

这些严重的过失已受到全国执行委员会的谴责，但该委员会要么不愿意，要么无法替换或惩处责任人。拉姆齐·麦克唐纳先生宣称印度是一个“非党派”问题，并使托利党帝国主义者认可了印度政策中的分母因素。

继他之后的人进一步延续了这一传统，并赢得了对面帝国主义者的赞赏。汉萨德议事录对此提供了充分的证明。

然而，全国执行委员会迄今为止一直避免公开承诺这样一种立场，即“工党政策”与社会主义原则在应用于印度时之间存在固有的矛盾。

目前的决定标志着一个明确的变化。我不得不得出不可避免的结论，即这一变化并非源于我的政治立场——这是一个恒定因素——而是源于全国执行委员会现在认为有必要宣布的立场变化。

它与帝国主义者的联系越紧密，就必须越努力驱赶那些反对帝国主义、反对人剥削人以及国剥削国的人。

这就是你们决定的寓意。全国执行委员会选择在此时此刻作出这一决定，使这一点显得尤为突出。无论是委员会还是其任何成员，都没有认为有必要对印度最杰出的社会主义者贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁潘迪特所遭受的严酷判决提出抗议。

全国执行委员会决定的影响深远，不仅涉及印度或我本人——其直接对象。它们挑战了社会主义者的信念。它们打击了国际社会主义的根基。

全国执行委员会现在已在劳工运动中引入了民族和种族壁垒。

在政治上，全国执行委员会现已毫无疑问地宣布，它对自己所谓的“印度人民福利”有其自身的概念，而这一概念与那些在它看来对印度负有“民族效忠”的人的概念是不相容的。换句话说，工党政策现在被其最高执行机构宣布为反对被统治民族自决和民族独立的基本概念，至多是一种仁慈且居高临下的帝国主义形式。

结束帝国主义及其伴随的贫困、剥削、种族仇恨、战争、致命的道德败坏和仇恨以及对思想的毒害，既是本国人民关切之事，也是马来亚、印度或非洲人民关切之事。

人民的“自然效忠”并不会分裂他们；相反，他们在共同的斗争中团结在一起，社会主义者应当承认并欢迎这种团结。以不同手段剥削所有人的共同敌人试图分裂他们。这也是其手段的一部分。

因此，令人惋惜的是，作为社会主义国际主要组成机构的英国工党全国执行委员会误导了自己，采用了帝国主义的范畴，并将自己置于其盟友的角色。

得知并相信全国执行委员会提出的这一奇怪学说不会在运动内部得到普遍接受，我感到鼓舞和勇气。

我很幸运能与劳工运动中的大量男女分享同志情谊，并接受他们的友谊和信任，我确信他们不会理解或接受你们的学说。因为他们完全相信，即使并不总是有机会去理解，你们所指的“效忠”源于我们共同的愿望，是我们对抗共同敌人的共同斗争的一部分。

我现在比以往任何时候都更清楚地认识到，全国执行委员会与其所代表的人之间存在着广泛且日益扩大的鸿沟。对于后者，我将毫无保留地提供我所能提供的服务。在他们心中，他们不承认你们的界限。

关于印度，我的立场保持不变。我对我的效忠无悔。我将继续努力，使人们认识到，各地人民的斗争是针对共同敌人的共同斗争，他们的剥削者试图分裂和削弱他们，而他们的力量在于团结。

幸运的是，在印度，这种观点得到了广泛的认识。印度人民与本国人民没有争执。他们的斗争是针对一个剥削和压迫的制度。即使在第二次工党政府残酷镇压的日子里，印度的民族运动也严格区分了当时对英国在印度政策负责的人和他们声称要代表的人。

我并非没有希望，时间、事件，最重要的是人民，将铸就那种统一——这是他们的敌人所恐惧和征服的。

怀着这种希望，我生活并奋斗。
此致，（签名），
V. K. 克里希纳·梅农
1930年12月28日。

事由 《字林西报》（China Press）—— 1941年2月22日在国际饭店为新闻界人士举行的鸡尾酒会。

Constable Is
Dismissed
Amid Scandal

Amid a hushed-up scandal
over the unexpected leniency
granted him by the First Special
District Court, the Chinese
constable who shot at Sub-
Inspector B. I. Kourjansky on
Friday was dismissed from the
Shanghai Municipal Police fol-
lowing his trial, THE CHINA
PRESS learned yesterday.

Although high police officers
remained non-committal on the
score, it was reported by reliable
sources that the constable was
sentenced to only 30 days' impri-
sonment—with an alternative of
paying $1 per day for his jail
term—in order to avert a threaten-
ed police strike.

Chinese constables of the
S.M.P., and of Bubbling Well
Station especially, were said
to have been in an agitated
frame of mind over the inci-
dent. Fears were rampant that
they would call a sympathy
strike should the arrested con-
stable receive the heavy sen-
tence which was expected in
view of the seriousness of his
offense.

The incident occurred Friday
evening. Angered when the Sub-
Inspector took his number down for
neglecting his duties on Kissehow
Road, near Sinza Road, the con-
stable cursed the Russian officer
and blocked his path when the
latter tried to return to the station.
He then drew his service pistol,
and pumped a shell into the bar-
rel. In the ensuing tussle a shot
rang out. Sub-Inspector Kourjansky
wrested the gun from the constable
and escorted him to the station.

Contrary to previous reports,
however, Sub-Inspector Kourjan-
sky was not wounded in the scuf-
fle.

华籍巡捕
在丑闻中被开除

据《字林西报》昨日获悉，一名华籍巡捕在周五枪击副督察B. I. 库尔江斯基（Kourjansky），在第一特区法院出乎意料地对其从轻发落引发了一场被压制的丑闻后，该巡捕在受审后被上海公共租界工部局警务处开除。

尽管高级警务官员对此事保持不置可否的态度，但可靠消息来源称，为避免发生迫在眉睫的警察罢工，该巡捕仅被判处30天监禁——或选择按每天1美元支付罚金以抵刑期。

据说，上海公共租界工部局警务处的华籍巡捕，特别是静安寺捕房的巡捕，对此事件情绪激动。人们普遍担心，如果被捕巡捕受到与其罪行严重性相称的预期重判，他们将发起同情性罢工。

事件发生在周五晚上。当副督察因该巡捕在新闸路附近基佐路（Kissehow Road，音译）玩忽职守而记下其警号时，该巡捕大怒，辱骂这位俄国警官，并在后者试图返回捕房时阻挡其去路。随后他拔出配枪，将一颗子弹推入枪膛。在随后的扭打中，一声枪响。库尔江斯基副督察从巡捕手中夺过枪支，并将其押送至捕房。

然而，与此前的报道相反，库尔江斯基副督察在扭打中并未受伤。

C. P. C. 2725 FACING
SURE DISMISSAL

Constable Found Guilty
Of Intimidation In
Court Hearing

Chinese Constable 2725, who was
found guilty of intimidating Sub-
Inspector B.I. Kourjansky of Bub-
bling Well Station in a violent al-
tercation on January 10, was ex-
pected to be dismissed from the
service yesterday, although no de-
finite line of administrative action
was as yet instituted.

This information was released by
S.M.P. Headquarters yesterday
morning, stating that, in conformity
with established precedent follow-
ed by the S.M.P., any member of
the police, found guilty of in-
timidating a superior officer, will
have to be removed from the
Force.

Judicial action had been taken
against the erring constable on
Saturday in the First Special Dis-
trict Court, where he was sentenced
to 30 days' imprisonment, suspend-
ed for three years. The decision
was regarded in police quarters as
an act of leniency on the accused,
considering the fact that he had
intended to use a weapon against a
superior officer.

In this connection, however,
S.M.P. Headquarters denied yester-
day that Sub-Inspector Kourjansky
was wounded. It was stated that
while a shot had been fired, nobody
was hurt. This fact was believed
to have been an extenuating cir-
cumstance that impelled the Judge
to take a lenient view of the in-
timidation.

C. P. C. 2725 面临
必然被开除

巡捕在庭审中被判
恐吓罪名成立

华籍巡捕2725号因在1月10日的暴力冲突中恐吓静安寺捕房副督察B.I. 库尔江斯基而被判有罪，预计昨日将被开除出警队，尽管尚未采取明确的行政行动。

上海公共租界工部局警务处总部昨日上午发布了这一消息，称按照上海公共租界工部局警务处遵循的既定先例，任何被判恐吓上级警官罪名成立的警务人员，都必须被清除出警队。

周六，第一特区法院对这名犯错巡捕采取了司法行动，判处其监禁30天，缓刑三年。鉴于该巡捕曾意图对上级使用武器，警方内部认为这一判决是对被告的宽大处理。

然而，就此而言，上海公共租界工部局警务处总部昨日否认库尔江斯基副督察受伤。声明称，虽然开了一枪，但无人受伤。这一事实被认为是一个减轻情节，促使法官对恐吓行为采取宽大看法。

Of The National Flag

proudly through the first year of
the Philippine Revolution, was
furled on December 27, 1897, when
the pact of Biak-Na-Bato was
signed, according to the terms of
which revolutionists laid down
their arms. A change was made
in the design at the Naic Revolu-
tionary Conference of March 17,
1897 when the letter "K" was
removed and the sun given a
mythological face.

The Filipino flag assumed its
present form early in 1898, as
designed and adopted by the Junta
Patriotica, the council of exiled
Filipino leaders at Hongkong, and
was brought home to Manila by
General Aguinaldo on May 19,
1898. In many a battle that fol-
lowed the return of the exiles, the
flag made more symbolical by the
addition of three stars represent-
ing the three major regions of the
Philippines, was borne triumphant-
ly by Aguinaldo's men.

OFFICIALLY UNFURLED
ON JUNE 12, 1898

It was officially unfurled and
declared the flag of the Philippine
Republic on June 12, 1898, at
Kawit, and it witnessed the inaug-
uration of the Republic at Malolos,
Bulacan, on June 23, 1899. The
same flag saw victory as well as
defeat in the Filipino-American
War until the capture of General
Aguinaldo by the Americans at
Palanan, Isabela, on March 23,
1901.

During the first years of the
American Occupation, the display

of the Filipino colors produced
such repercussions that the Phi-
lippine Commission, on August 28,
1907, passed Act No. 1696 other-
wise known as the Flag Law,
which forbade the display of the
flag anywhere, even in Filipino
homes. During every legislative
session from 1908 to 1914, efforts
were exerted by Filipino leaders to
secure the repeal of that law, and
success came when a bill to this
effect was signed on October 22,
1919, by Governor-General Francis
Burton Harrison.

The restoration of the colors
to the people in effect marked the
recognition of Filipino nationality,
and today the Filipino Flag waves
side by side with the Stars and
Stripes, symbol of a new freedom
and a new nation. Sergio Osmeña,
Filipino leader, once wrote:

"The sun still speaks of a new
nation which yesterday was born
in liberty, amidst the roar of can-
non, the confusion and the tumult
of conflict, and today advances
peacefully and surely along the
path of constitutional liberty....
The white still tells of our peace-
ful and friendly purpose as well as
the sincerity and purity of our
action; the red still proclaims the
indomitable energy with which we
hold on to our convictions; and the
blue, that which represents the
stainless blue of our aspirations
still represents our ideal of nation-
ality—pure, intact, unimpaired,
undefiled by any cloud whatever
in the firmament of our national
sovereignty."

关于国旗

在菲律宾革命的第一年中自豪地飘扬，根据比亚克纳巴托（Biak-Na-Bato）条约的条款，革命者放下武器，该旗帜于1897年12月27日降下。1897年3月17日，在奈克（Naic）革命会议上，旗帜设计发生了变更，去掉了字母“K”，并为太阳赋予了神话般的面孔。

菲律宾国旗于1898年初采用了现在的形式，由流亡香港菲律宾领导人委员会“爱国 junta”（Junta Patriotica）设计并通过，并于1898年5月19日由阿吉纳尔多将军带回马尼拉。在流亡者归来后的许多战斗中，这面旗帜因增加了代表菲律宾三个主要地区的三颗星而更具象征意义，由阿吉纳尔多的部下胜利地高举。

于1898年6月12日正式展开

1898年6月12日，它在卡维特（Kawit）正式展开并被宣布为菲律宾共和国的国旗，并见证了1899年6月23日在布拉干省马洛洛斯（Malolos, Bulacan）举行的共和国成立典礼。同一面旗帜见证了菲美战争中的胜利与失败，直到1901年3月23日阿吉纳尔多将军在伊莎贝拉省帕拉南（Palanan, Isabela）被美军俘虏。

在美国占领的最初几年，展示菲律宾色彩引发了如此强烈的反响，以至于菲律宾委员会于1907年8月28日通过了第1696号法案，即所谓的《旗帜法》，禁止在任何地方展示该旗帜，甚至包括菲律宾人的家中。从1908年到1914年的每一次立法会议期间，菲律宾领导人都努力争取废除该法律，直到1919年10月22日总督弗朗西斯·伯顿·哈里森（Francis Burton Harrison）签署了相关法案，才取得成功。

将色彩归还给人民，实际上标志着对菲律宾民族性的承认，如今菲律宾国旗与星条旗并肩飘扬，象征着新的自由和新的国家。菲律宾领导人塞尔吉奥·奥斯梅尼亚（Sergio Osmeña）曾写道：

“太阳仍然诉说着一个新国家的诞生，它昨天在自由中诞生，伴随着大炮的轰鸣、冲突的混乱和喧嚣，今天则在宪政自由的道路上和平而坚定地前进……白色仍然讲述着我们和平友好的意图，以及我们行动的真诚与纯洁；红色仍然宣告着我们坚持信念的不屈能量；而蓝色，代表我们 aspirations（愿望/抱负）的纯净蓝色，仍然代表着我们的民族理想——纯洁、完整、无损，在我们国家主权的天空中没有任何云彩的玷污。”

NEWS BEHIND
THE NEWS

Defection
In the present state of mind and mood of the
American community, it is a wonder that the high-
ranking official in the local branch of one of the
American banks does not suffer social excommunica-
tion or some other more violent fate for his enthusi-
astic pro-Nazi leanings.
He was reported the other day to have been
seen in all the glory of a party shirt, sticking his
arm out with the rest of them.

Spy Department
AN interesting sidelight on the recent successful
bombing of Italian Naval units in Taranto
harbor was the announcement that some of the Bri-
tish planes were operating from the aircraft carrier
Illustrious.
The Illustrious was one of the five 23,000-
ton aircraft laid down in England before the pre-
sent war began. Belonging as they do to the
same building program, they would presumably
all be finished about the same time, and there-
fore this first official intimation of the entry of
the Illustrious into active service probably means
that the war strength of aircraft carriers has
been increased by five, which cancels out very
handsomely the loss of the Courageous and the
Glorious.
The five battleships of the King George V class,
35,000 tons, are also rumored to be on active service
now, bringing the total battle line to 19 ships, with
the two giant Temeraires, 42,000 tons, nearing com-
pletion.
The Italians will have to think about turning
their three remaining battleships into submarines.
They would be in their element there at least.

（印：BRANCH）

新闻背后的
新闻

叛变
鉴于目前美国侨民群体的心态和情绪，令人惊讶的是，当地一家美国银行分行的高级官员因其热情的亲纳粹倾向，竟未遭受社交圈的排斥或其他更激烈的后果。
据报道，日前有人看见他身穿政党衬衫，与其他人一样伸出手臂行纳粹礼，神气活现。

间谍部门
关于近期英国飞机成功轰炸塔兰托港意大利海军舰艇一事，一个有趣的侧面消息是，公告称部分英国飞机是从“光辉”号 (Illustrious) 航空母舰上起飞的。
“光辉”号是目前战争爆发前在英国铺设龙骨的五艘23,000吨级航空母舰之一。由于它们属于同一建造计划，预计完工时间大致相同，因此，“光辉”号正式投入现役的首次暗示可能意味着航空母舰的战备力量增加了五艘，这很好地抵消了“勇敢”号 (Courageous) 和“光荣”号 (Glorious) 的损失。
据传，五艘35,000吨级的“乔治五世国王”级战列舰也已投入现役，使战列舰总数达到19艘，而两艘42,000吨级的巨型“无畏”号 (Temeraires) 也即将完工。
意大利人将不得不考虑将其剩余的三艘战列舰改装为潜艇。至少在那里，它们能如鱼得水。

（印：处）

JUN 1 8 1940

Views Mechanization
Gen. Kimura
Arrives To
Inspect Army

Major-General Seiichi Kimura, adviser to the Kawasaki Rolling Stock Company, and eight other officials of leading industrial companies in Japan were among the 455 passengers of the N.Y.K. liner Tatsuta Maru which arrived here Sunday afternoon, the Tairiku Shimpo reported yesterday.

Major-General Kimura and others will visit Central China fronts to inspect Japanese mechanized units. During their two-month tour of Central China fronts, they will collect material which may lead to an improvement in the nation's mechanized force, the paper said.

Mr. Sadao Iguchi, sectional chief of the Information Bureau of the Foreign Office, who was recently appointed Japanese Consul-General at New York, also arrived on board the Tatsuta Maru.

"I want to see the Far East before I assume my new post in the United States. During my current inspection tour, I intend to visit South China, and Hongkong as well as the Philippines," Mr. Iguchi told a representative of the Tairiku Shimpo upon his arrival here.

CHINA PRESS.

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

Bryan's Pay Check
The Shanghai Municipal Council has announced that, in order to retain the services of Mr. Robert T. Bryan, Jr., Municipal Advocate, it has been necessary to pay that individual an annual salary of U$7,500. Because of his special talents, namely his knowledge of Chinese civil and criminal law, Mr. Bryan is an important cog in the Settlement administration. But there are a lot of people who will question the point as to whether he is important enough to warrant paying him a salary of US$7,500 in times as hard as there. When you consider the fact that 3,000 P.W.D. coolies were permitted to strike because they wanted an increase of around 20 cents per day (they got 18 cents, or about US$3.40 annually per man), one starts to wonder whether the S.M.C. still has the correct slant on the salary question.

The argument, of course, is that you can get coolie at a few dollars a dozen while key men are hard to find. This is true but only to a certain extent. I never fool myself into believing that, given the chance, another man could not handle my job as well, if not better, than myself. Nor do I kid myself into believing that the dime a dozen boys who serve under me could not upset the whole apple-cart if the idea entered their heads. The point is that 3,000 low-paid coolies can throw the health of this city into jeopardy over a few bowls of rice. And that's when the public starts to lose faith in its key men.

I agree that department heads should receive substantial salaries, even in foreign currency, if it is necessary. But it also seems to me that question of how much these salaries should be deserves a great deal of consideration. Three years ago, a salary of US$7,500 for the S.M.C. municipal advocate, would have looked excessive. But today, it does.

（批：Rul p? 5/4 2a）

《字林西报》。

我常常在想 作者：卡罗尔·D·奥尔科特 (CARROLL D. ALCOTT)

布莱恩的薪水支票
上海公共租界工部局宣布，为了留住市政律师小罗伯特·T·布莱恩 (Robert T. Bryan, Jr.) 先生，有必要支付此人每年7,500美元的薪水。由于其特殊才能，即精通中国民事和刑事法律，布莱恩先生是租界行政机构中的重要一环。但是，有许多人会质疑，在如此艰难的时世，他是否重要到值得支付7,500美元年薪的地步。当你考虑到这样一个事实，即3,000名工部局苦力因为要求每天加薪约20美分而被允许罢工（他们最终获得了18美分，即每人每年约3.40美元），人们开始怀疑工部局在薪资问题上是否仍持有正确的视角。

当然，论点在于，你可以以几美元一打的价格雇到苦力，而关键人才却很难找到。这在一定程度上是正确的。我从不自欺欺人地认为，如果有机会，其他人不能像我一样好，甚至更好地处理我的工作。我也不自欺欺人地认为，在我手下那些廉价的小伙子们如果动起念头来，不会搞砸整个局面。关键在于，3,000名低薪苦力可能会因为几碗饭的问题而危及这座城市的卫生状况。而这正是公众开始对其关键人物失去信心的时候。

我同意，如果有必要，各部门主管应获得丰厚的薪水，即使是外币。但在我看来，这些薪水究竟应该定为多少，也值得深思。三年前，工部局市政律师7,500美元的薪水看起来可能过高。但今天，确实如此。

（批注：Rul p? 5/4 2a）

The China Press
BULLETIN
SHANGHAI, THURSDAY, AUGUST 17, 1939
Habeas Corpus Writ
Rejected By Court

In a decision historical in its implications, and possibly far-reaching in its effects, Judge P. Grant Jones in H. M. Supreme Court for China today rejected an application for a writ of habeas corpus in the case of the four Chinese being detained by the British Municipal authorities in Tientsin.

Reflecting the determination of the parties who have interested themselves in the case, however, it was learned by THE CHINA PRESS that immediately after the decision had been handed down, machinery was set in motion for an appeal to be lodged.

The case will be contested to the highest legal authorities in the British Empire, the Privy Council, if necessary, it was declared.

World-wide interest was aroused by the application, which, as exclusively reported in THE CHINA PRESS Sunday, was made to Judge P. Grant Jones by Messrs. H. A. Reeks and J. R. Jones, representing Messrs. Ellis and Hayes, on cabled instruction from Messrs. Elwell and Binford Hole, of London.

The application brought to a dramatic climax the steadily increasing opposition in England to the British Government's decision to hand the four Chinese over to the Japanese authorities, for subsequent trial by the puppet court of the Peiping regime.

Messrs. Elwell and Binford Hole were acting on behalf of Mr. Norman Bentwich, Professor of International Law at the Jerusalem University and former attorney-general in Palestine, and Miss M. Fry, a Justice of the Peace and a director of the British Broadcasting Corporation. Professor Bentwich and Miss Fry were foremost in the movement which swiftly gathered force in England in opposition to the Government.

Dramatic Action

Although it had been announced previously in England that Miss Fry and Professor Bentwich would take legal action to challenge the Government's decision, the instructions received by Messrs. Ellis and Hayes in Shanghai arrived dramatically Friday night and it was not until late on Saturday that the information first leaked out that the application had been heard in Chambers before Judge Grant Jones.

In view of the far-reaching effects the decision of the Court must have, it was thought in Shanghai that His Lordship would consult the highest possible authorities before announcing his decision, although at the same time, it was thought that the urgency of the situation would necessitate an early finding.

It will be recalled that the four Chinese were detained by the British authorities in Tientsin following the assassination of Cheng Szu-kang, a Customs Superintendent, who was killed in a Tientsin cinema on April 3.

Although on a previous occasion a Chinese captured by the Tientsin British authorities on suspicion that he had been engaged in terroristic activities was handed over to the Japanese authorities on the completion of investigations, the British resolutely refused until last week to surrender the four men detained on suspicion that they had been connected with the murder of Cheng.

Blockade Started

It was held by the Tientsin authorities that the evidence supplied by the Japanese was not conclusive, but the authorities subsequently agreed to detain the men pending further investigations.

As a result of the British refusal to surrender the four men, a virtual military blockade of Tientsin by the Japanese was precipitated, with consequent indignities inflicted on British subjects who were compelled to pass the Japanese barriers.

The current negotiations in Tokyo between Sir Robert Craigie and the Japanese authorities were instituted in an effort by Britain to reach a solution to the problem and late last week, the British Government finally instructed Sir Robert to agree to the surrender of the men, although at the same time it was stressed that the handing-over was agreed to only because new evidence supplied by the Japanese was regarded by the Government as being satisfactory.

Outcry Raised

An immediate outcry was raised by the British press, conservative, liberal and socialist alike, and the movement grew to proportions described in recently arrived cables from England as "greatly embarrassing to Mr. Chamberlain's Government."

In their application to Judge Grant Jones Saturday, Messrs. Reeks and Jones requested that the writ be directed to the British Municipal Police in Tientsin, the two institutions of the proceedings holding that the four men could be tried only by the properly recognized courts in China.

上海，1939年8月17日，星期四

人身保护令状
被法院驳回

在一项具有历史意义且可能产生深远影响的裁决中，英国在华最高法院法官P. Grant Jones今日驳回了关于四名被天津英租界当局拘押的华人申请人身保护令状的申请。

然而，据《字林西报》获悉，鉴于各方对此案的关注与决心，在裁决下达后，立即启动了提出上诉的程序。

据称，如有必要，此案将一直上诉至大英帝国的最高司法机构——枢密院。

此项申请引起了全世界的关注。正如《字林西报》周日独家报道的那样，该申请由H. A. Reeks先生和J. R. Jones先生代表Ellis and Hayes律师事务所，根据伦敦Elwell and Binford Hole律师事务所的电报指示，向P. Grant Jones法官提出。

这一申请使英国国内反对英国政府决定将这四名华人移交给日本当局、随后由北平伪政权傀儡法庭审判的日益增长的反对情绪达到了戏剧性的高潮。

Elwell and Binford Hole律师事务所是代表耶路撒冷大学国际法教授、前巴勒斯坦总检察长Norman Bentwich先生，以及太平绅士、英国广播公司董事M. Fry女士行事的。Bentwich教授和Fry女士在英国迅速兴起并壮大的反对政府的运动中处于领先地位。

戏剧性行动

尽管此前已在英国宣布Fry女士和Bentwich教授将采取法律行动挑战政府的决定，但Ellis and Hayes律师事务所在上海收到的指示直到周五晚上才戏剧性地到达，直到周六晚些时候，消息才首次泄露出来，即该申请已在Grant Jones法官的内庭进行了审理。

鉴于法院的裁决必然会产生深远的影响，上海方面认为，法官阁下在宣布裁决之前会咨询尽可能最高级别的当局，但同时也认为，局势的紧迫性要求尽早作出裁定。

回顾一下，这四名华人是在海关监督程锡庚（Cheng Szu-kang）于4月3日在天津一家电影院遇刺身亡后，被天津英国当局拘留的。

虽然在此前的一次事件中，一名被天津英国当局因涉嫌参与恐怖活动而抓获的华人在调查结束后被移交给日本当局，但直到上周，英国方面坚决拒绝移交因涉嫌与程锡庚谋杀案有关而被拘留的四名男子。

封锁开始

天津当局认为日本方面提供的证据并不确凿，但当局随后同意在进一步调查期间拘留这些人。

由于英国拒绝移交这四名男子，导致日本对天津实施了事实上的军事封锁，致使英国臣民在通过日本关卡时遭受了相应的侮辱。

罗伯特·克雷吉爵士（Sir Robert Craigie）与日本当局在东京进行的当前谈判，是英国为寻求解决这一问题而发起的努力。上周晚些时候，英国政府最终指示罗伯特爵士同意移交这些人，但同时强调，之所以同意移交，仅仅是因为政府认为日本提供的新证据令人满意。

引起强烈抗议

英国新闻界立即发出了强烈抗议，无论是保守派、自由派还是社会主义派报刊均如此，这场运动的发展规模，根据最近从英国发来的电报描述，已“使张伯伦先生（Mr. Chamberlain）的政府极为尴尬”。

在周六向Grant Jones法官提出的申请中，Reeks和Jones两位先生请求将令状指向天津英租界巡捕房，诉讼双方均认为，这四名男子只能由中国正式认可的法庭进行审判。

CHINA PRESS - 29.10.37.
26971

S.M.C. Anxious
Not To Stir Up
Political Feud

“Alleyway Associations”
Frowned On; Papers
Told To Register

Determined to keep the International Settlement a safe place of refuge for Chinese and foreign people, the Shanghai Municipal Council has taken the view that it will not tolerate the existence of any radical political organizations which attempt to stir up civic unrest under the guise of patriotism. THE CHINA PRESS was informed yesterday.

In this connection, the Council has frowned on attempts to organize the residents of the lanes and alleys into units known as the “Alleyway Associations.” While willing to deal liberally with such organizations, the Council fears that the promoters are likely to use patriotic fervor to create situations which may seriously endanger the peace and order of the Settlement.

The Shanghai Municipal Police, it is understood, has been instructed to use its discretion in preventing meetings of “Alleyway Associations.”

Meantime, the Council’s stand regarding Chinese political activities in the Settlement remains unchanged. Legitimate organizations will not be interfered with in their attempts to direct and organize the patriotic activities of the Chinese community, it was pointed out.

The decision on banning the “Alleyway Associations” and other radical organizations, it is learned, was taken before the sudden turn in the local war situation. The withdrawal of Chinese troops from Chapei and Kiangwan, the reporter was assured, will not affect in any respect the Council’s original stand to keep the International Settlement a neutral area, wherein people of all nationalities will be accorded protection.

At the same time, the Council has also issued orders for all local Chinese newspapers to register. This step was also taken, to prevent irresponsible persons from utilizing a powerful propaganda implement in creating unrest. Legitimate Chinese papers will continue to enjoy every freedom in their editorial policies, THE CHINA PRESS was assured.

《大陆报》- 1937年10月29日。
26971

工部局焦急地
不愿挑起
政治争端

“里弄协会”
遭冷遇；报纸
被令注册

据昨日《大陆报》获悉，上海公共租界工部局决心将国际租界维持为中外人士的安全避难所，因此认为不能容忍任何企图以爱国为幌子煽动市民动荡的激进政治组织存在。

对此，工部局对试图将里弄居民组织成称为“里弄协会”的单位之举表示不赞成。虽然工部局愿意宽容对待此类组织，但担心发起者可能利用爱国热情制造局势，从而严重危及租界的和平与秩序。

据悉，上海公共租界警务处已获指示，运用其裁量权阻止“里弄协会”的集会。

同时，工部局关于租界内华人政治活动的立场保持不变。据指出，合法组织在指导和组织华人社区爱国活动方面的尝试不会受到干涉。

据了解，禁止“里弄协会”及其他激进组织的决定是在当地战局突然转变之前作出的。记者得到保证，中国军队从闸北和江湾的撤退，绝不会在任何方面影响工部局保持国际租界为中立的原有立场，在该区域内，所有国籍的人民都将受到保护。

与此同时，工部局还下令所有本地中文报纸进行注册。采取这一措施也是为了防止不负责任之人利用强有力的宣传工具制造动荡。《大陆报》得到保证，合法的中文报纸将继续在其编辑方针上享有充分的自由。

（批：《大陆报》注册了吗？）
（批：B）
（批：D.E. S/S 10月29日）
（批：S.I. 提请 D.S. 注意 10月29日）

In blindly carrying on the war of resistance, 
the Chungking regime is unhesitatingly using the nation and 
the people as the stakes. It is laying hands on the capital 
of the people by recklessly issuing paper notes, thereby 
causing inflation and raising commodity prices. The value 
of the legal tender has been declining daily until to-day $1 
Zegal tender has the purchasing power of only 40 cents. 

After its reorganization and return to Nanking, 
the National Government has decided to establish a Central 
Bank and to issue currency to assist the development of 
industry and commerce. On this account, the legal tender 
of the Chungking regime registered a further decline and this 
has caused the rich to change their legal temer fof foreign 
currency. 

The sharp decline in the value of legal tender 
gave rise yesterday to unprecedented changes in the local 
money market. At noon the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking 
Corporation and the Chartered Bank of Australia, India and 
China refused to accept legal tender for the purchase of U.S. 

llars or sterling, because the stabilization fund in 

ngkong was already exhausted. Disagreement also exists 

etween T.V. Soong and the Chungking regime because of the 
latter's tolerance of the Communist Party. The economic 
collapse of the Chungking regime is certain; it is a 
reflection of the war weariness of the people and their 
longing for peace. 

The confusion existing in the local money 
market is due to the inability of the Chungking to maintain 
its financial policy and to the prevalence of internal strife 
among its own factions, The British and American authorities 
entertain certain suspicions of the Chungking regime and have 
ceased rendering further assistance. This has caused great 
apprehension to the Chungking regime and created a panic in 
Shanghai. 

Some attribute yesterday's sharp decline in 
the value of the legal tender to the extension of the European 
War; others say that Britain has suffered a heavy reverse}; 
many declare that the Chungking regime is going to issue gold 
reserve notes and that it will cease maintaining the exchange 
market in Shanghai. Nobody mows the truth and even the banks 
are waiting for the quotations of the Hongkong and Shanghai 
Banking Corporation.

Sir, 

The editor of the Dah Chung News Agency, 
Mr. Chen Ting Hwei, was interviewed by me at 
headquarters this morning regarding the publication 
of an article entitled “Rice Situation in Shanghai” 
which appeared in four Chinese language newspapers 
on June 18, 1940. He stated that che article was 
the result of an interview he had with Mr. Yu Ya Ching. 
As Mr. Yu did not wish his name to be published as 
being the source of this article, he, the editor, 
announced that the information was secured from the 
Rice Hong Owners Guild. Regarding the speculators 
mentioned, he stated that no particular persons were 
indicated and that he intended it to refer to specu- 
lators in general. He added that his reference to 
rumours by undesirables was included in order to allay 
the fears of the public regarding the possible increase 
in the price of rice. Statement attached. 


(Sd.) J. Mason.

Owing to the heavy increase in the price of rice 
which seriously affects the livelihood of the people, I had 
an interview with Mr. Yu Ya-ching at the Navigation Club on 
the afternoon of June 17. 

According to Mr. Yu, there is no reason for the price 
of rice to be increased because of the favourable rate of 
foreign exchange; furthermore large quantities of foreign rice 
have already been ordered. It is evident that the increase 
is due to persons, in possession of idle capital, manipulating 
or speculating in rice. 

As Mr. Yu is a prominent merchant in this locality, 
his statement might put an end to rumours and also pacify the 
minds of the people. I, therefore, wrote the article in 
question. As I had not secured his approval beforehand, I 
stated in my article that the report had been secured from 
a member of the Rice Hong Owners’ Guild. 

My intention in writing the article in question was 
to appease the minds of the people in Shanghai. Morsvver, 

Mr. Yu had also approved it when I showed him the text. 


(Chopped and signed) Chen Ting-huei.
